classes.qualifier-missing-from-name: the definition adds an identifying attribute the name lacks (normalisation, a vector or component where the name states a scalar, an ion-only population where the name states an element, a reference-relative value, an equivalent-electron count, an averaged form, extra weighting), so the name alone denotes a broader or different quantity
classes.definition-narrower-than-name: the definition restricts applicability to a subset of the objects the name covers (a coil family, an instrument, a plasma regime or surface, a layer)
classes.abstract-parent-as-quantity: the definition declares a parent, umbrella or structural quantity whose population, component, averaging or specialised forms are fixed by more specific instances
classes.unit-does-not-fit-name: the unit's physical dimension contradicts the quantity the name states
classes.agrees: the definition states the same scope the name states

items.name: ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface
items.description:
Cumulative wave power absorbed by a specified ion charge state, integrated
over the plasma volume enclosed by a selected magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative power associated with one physically defined
plasma heating or energy-transfer channel inside a specified magnetic flux
surface. Here, the channel is absorption of wave energy by one specified ion
charge state, and the ion population may be thermal or fast.

The cumulative absorbed power is

$$
P_{q,a}(\psi) = \int_{V(\psi)} p^{\mathrm{abs}}_{q,a}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{q,a}(\psi)$ is the cumulative absorbed wave power, $q$ identifies
the ion charge state, $a$ identifies the thermal or fast ion population,
$\psi$ is the magnetic-flux-surface label, $V(\psi)$ is the enclosed plasma
volume, $p^{\mathrm{abs}}_{q,a}$ is the corresponding volumetric wave-power
absorption density, $\mathbf{r}$ is position, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is the
volume element.

This quantity is the charge-state-resolved specialization of [power at
inside flux surface](name:power_at_inside_flux_surface). It excludes power
absorbed by other charge states and power that is launched but not absorbed;
corresponding thermal and fast instances are [thermal ion charge-state power
at inside flux
surface](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface) and
[fast ion charge-state power at inside flux
surface](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

items.name: ion_current_density
items.description:
Ion current density is the vector density of conventional electric charge
flux carried by ions, obtained by charge-weighting their directed particle
motion across unit area.
items.documentation:
Ion current density $\mathbf{J}_i$ is the vector density of conventional
electric charge flux carried by ions. It represents signed charge transport
from all included ion species and charge states.

The kinetic definition is the charge-weighted first velocity moment of the
ion distribution functions:

$$
\mathbf{J}_i(\mathbf{x},t) = \sum_{s\in\mathrm{ions}} q_s \int \mathbf{v}\,f_s(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v},t)\,d^3v = \sum_{s\in\mathrm{ions}} q_s n_s \mathbf{u}_s
$$

where $\mathbf{x}$ is position, $t$ is time, $s$ indexes ion species and
charge states, $q_s$ is the charge of population $s$, $\mathbf{v}$ is
particle velocity, $f_s$ is its velocity-space distribution function, $n_s$
is its number density, and $\mathbf{u}_s$ is its mean velocity.

This quantity includes ion-carried charge flux and excludes electron-carried
and displacement-current density. Its qualified instances may select a
magnetic-field-aligned projection such as [parallel ion current
density](name:parallel_ion_current_density), a temporal fluctuation measure
such as [fluctuating ion current
density](name:fluctuating_ion_current_density), or an ion-saturation
collection condition.

Sign convention: Positive when an ion-carried charge-flux component is
aligned with the positive direction of its defining basis vector or oriented
surface normal.

items.name: oxygen_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Particle number density of oxygen ions at the internal transport barrier,
the flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent
transport permits steep radial impurity density gradients to form; summed
over all oxygen ionization states and excluding neutral oxygen.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of oxygen ions at the internal transport barrier is
the local oxygen-ion particle density on the flux surface selected as the
barrier reference location. The internal transport barrier (ITB) is a
confined-plasma region where locally reduced cross-field turbulent transport
can sustain steep gradients in density, temperature, and pressure. Oxygen
(atomic number $Z = 8$) is a low-$Z$ impurity; this species-level quantity
is summed over all oxygen ion charge states and excludes neutral oxygen
atoms.

The local oxygen-ion number density $n_\mathrm{O}$ at the ITB reference flux
label is the zeroth velocity moment of the aggregate oxygen-ion distribution
function $f_\mathrm{O}$:

$$
n_\mathrm{O}(\rho_\mathrm{ITB}) = \int f_\mathrm{O}(\mathbf{v},\, \rho_\mathrm{ITB})\, d^3v
$$

where $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, $\rho_\mathrm{ITB}$ is the
normalized minor-radius flux label identifying the ITB flux surface, and
$f_\mathrm{O}$ represents the combined ion population over oxygen charge
states.

At the elemental-species level, the aggregation convention is unweighted by
charge state: equivalently, $n_\mathrm{O} = \sum_{q=1}^{8}
n_{\mathrm{O}^{q+}}$, covering $\mathrm{O}^{1+}$ through fully stripped
$\mathrm{O}^{8+}$. This quantity is the oxygen-specific child of
[density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
and a specialization of ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier;
charge-state-resolved oxygen densities are distinct quantities.

items.name: resistivity_of_wall_material
items.description:
Electrical resistivity of wall material, relating local electric field to
current density and determining ohmic dissipation during electromagnetic
transients.
items.documentation:
Electrical resistivity is the local bulk material property that opposes
electric current in the wall and converts electromagnetic energy into heat.
It applies to the wall material at each physical location, with values
allowed to vary between material locations.

For an isotropic local response, resistivity is defined by

$$
\mathbf{E}(\mathbf{r}) = \rho(\mathbf{r})\,\mathbf{J}(\mathbf{r})
$$

where $\mathbf{E}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local electric-field vector,
$\mathbf{J}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local conventional current-density vector,
$\rho(\mathbf{r})$ is the local electrical resistivity, and $\mathbf{r}$
denotes physical position in the wall.

This quantity is a local bulk material property, not a wall-wide average, a
lumped current-path resistance, or an interface or contact resistance. It is
therefore distinct from the lumped [resistance of a vacuum
vessel](name:resistance_of_vacuum_vessel) and resistance of a passive
structure, which also depend on conductor geometry and current-path length.

The local irreversible heating density is $p_{\rm
ohm}=\mathbf{J}\cdot\mathbf{E}$, where $p_{\rm ohm}$ is ohmic power density;
integrating this density over the wall material gives the [power at the wall
due to ohmic dissipation](name:power_at_wall_due_to_ohmic_dissipation).

items.name: vertical_ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity
items.description:
Effective coefficient relating the convective flux of vertical momentum to
its density for one ion species and charge state in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the effective coefficient for advective, non-diffusive
transport of vertical [momentum](name:momentum) carried by a specified ion
species in one charge state. Vertical is parallel to the toroidal symmetry
axis in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

For a transport surface with a chosen positive unit normal $\hat{\mathbf
n}$, the convective flux of vertical momentum is defined by:

$$
\Pi^{\mathrm{conv}}_{s,Z} = V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{s,Z}\,g_{s,Z}
$$

where $s$ identifies the ion species and charge state,
$\Pi^{\mathrm{conv}}_{s,Z}$ is its convective vertical-momentum flux through
the surface along $\hat{\mathbf n}$, $V^{\mathrm{conv}}_{s,Z}$ is this
effective convection coefficient, and $g_{s,Z}$ is its vertical momentum
density.

The vertical label selects the transported momentum component; the transport
normal need not be vertical. The coefficient is charge-state resolved,
without summation or averaging over charge states. It is distinct from the
charge state's bulk vertical flow velocity and excludes gradient-driven
diffusive momentum transport.

It resolves the vertical momentum component of [ion charge-state momentum
convection velocity](name:ion_charge_state_momentum_convection_velocity) and
specializes [vertical momentum convection
velocity](name:vertical_momentum_convection_velocity) to the specified ion
species and charge state.

Sign convention: Positive when the convective flux along the chosen surface
normal has the same sign as the vertical momentum density, with positive
vertical momentum directed toward increasing $Z$.

items.name: x_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector
items.description:
Cartesian x component of the unit vector along the unshattered pellet
velocity immediately before shattering, resolved in the right-handed
Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the x-directed Cartesian component of the unit vector
aligned with the unshattered pellet velocity immediately before shattering.
It describes the injection direction associated with the pellet injector,
not a hardware-axis orientation or a post-shattering fragment direction.

The injection-direction vector is decomposed in the right-handed Cartesian
$(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis as

$$
\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{inj}}=u_x\hat{x}+u_y\hat{y}+u_z\hat{z},\qquad u_x=\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{inj}}\cdot\hat{x},\qquad |\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{inj}}|=1
$$

where $\mathbf{u}_{\mathrm{inj}}$ is the unshattered pellet
velocity-direction unit vector, $u_x$ is its x component, and $\hat{x}$,
$\hat{y}$, and $\hat{z}$ are the Cartesian basis unit vectors. The
corresponding components are given by the [y unit vector of the pellet
injector](name:y_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector) and [z direction unit
vector of the pellet
injector](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_pellet_injector).

items.name: radial_outline_of_ferritic_element
items.description:
Non-negative major-radius coordinate of a point on a ferritic element
outline in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Non-negative major-radius coordinate $R$ of a point on a ferritic element
outline in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame is the distance
of that point from the toroidal symmetry axis. It specializes the [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) to ferritic-element outline points and
is paired with the vertical outline coordinate for the same outline point.

The major radius is equivalently the norm of the horizontal Cartesian
position vector:

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are horizontal Cartesian coordinate components in the
right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis, with $\hat{z}$
parallel to the vertical direction $\hat{Z}$.

This coordinate denotes an outline-point location and is not a signed radial
displacement, aggregate radial size, centroid position, or maximum radial
boundary coordinate. The aggregate radial size is represented by [width of
ferritic element](name:width_of_ferritic_element), the centroid position by
[radial coordinate of ferritic element
centroid](name:radial_coordinate_of_ferritic_element_centroid), and the
maximum radial boundary coordinate by [outer radius of ferritic
element](name:outer_radius_of_ferritic_element).

items.name: toroidal_neutral_momentum_diffusivity
items.description:
Kinematic coefficient relating diffusive toroidal transport of a neutral
species' bulk momentum to its opposing toroidal momentum-density gradient.
items.documentation:
Toroidal neutral momentum diffusivity is the kinematic coefficient governing
diffusive transport of bulk neutral [momentum](name:momentum) along the
toroidal direction. It is the toroidal directional component of [neutral
momentum diffusivity](name:neutral_momentum_diffusivity). This direction
follows increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

In a local, componentwise Fick-law closure:

$$
\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{0,\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}} = -D_{0,\phi}\frac{1}{R}\frac{\partial \mathbf{g}_0}{\partial \phi}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\Pi}_{0,\phi}^{\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive flux of
neutral linear momentum across a surface normal to the toroidal direction,
$D_{0,\phi}$ is this diffusivity, and $\mathbf{g}_0$ is the bulk neutral
momentum density. The subscript $0$ denotes the neutral population. The
derivative is taken at fixed major radius and vertical height; the factor
$1/R$ converts differentiation with respect to toroidal angle into
differentiation along physical toroidal arc length.

The quantity applies to a specified neutral species with its internal states
combined, rather than to one resolved internal-state channel. Bulk momentum
density is summed over those states, but this effective coefficient is not
the sum of their diffusivities. The [toroidal neutral internal-state
momentum diffusion
coefficient](name:toroidal_neutral_internal_state_momentum_diffusion_coefficient)
instead applies to a resolved state. Charged-particle contributions are
excluded from the population, and the diffusive closure excludes convective
momentum transport, residual stress, and external momentum sources.

items.name: thermal_neutral_density
items.description:
Number density of neutral particles in the thermal population of a specified
atomic or molecular species, including all internal states but excluding
ions and nonthermal neutrals.
items.documentation:
Number density of neutral

At a given position and time, the density is defined by

$$
n_{s,0}^{\mathrm{th}} = \int f_{s,0}^{\mathrm{th}}(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_{s,0}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal neutral number density, $s$
labels the selected species, $0$ denotes zero electric charge, and the
superscript $\mathrm{th}$ identifies the thermal population. The function
$f_{s,0}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is that population's velocity distribution summed
over internal states, and $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity. The integral
covers all velocity space.

The quantity excludes ionized particles and fast or other nonthermal
neutrals. Different neutral species are not summed. The defining density is
local; spatial averaging, when applied, preserves these population
restrictions.

Summing the [thermal neutral internal-state
density](name:thermal_neutral_internal_state_density) over a complete set of
internal states recovers this quantity. It is the thermal contribution to
[neutral species density](name:neutral_species_density) for the same species
and contributes to [neutral density](name:neutral_density) when species and
population contributions are combined.

items.name: radial_total_ion_energy_flux
items.description:
Total ion energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces is the
flux-surface-averaged net energy transport per unit area and time, summed
over all ion species and charge states.
items.documentation:
Total ion energy flux across magnetic flux surfaces represents the net
transport of the aggregate ion energy reservoir through those surfaces. It
includes conductive thermal-energy transport and convective enthalpy or
bulk-kinetic transport.

The defining projection and averaging relation is:

$$
\Gamma_{W,i}^{\mathrm{tot}} = \left\langle \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,i}^{\mathrm{tot}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf n} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{W,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the flux-surface-averaged outward ion
energy flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_{W,i}^{\mathrm{tot}}$ is the local [total
ion energy-flux vector](name:total_ion_energy_flux), $\hat{\mathbf n}$ is
the outward unit normal to the magnetic flux surface, and
$\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{FS}}$ denotes a flux-surface average. The
labels $W$, $i$, and $\mathrm{tot}$ identify energy, ions, and the total ion
contribution, respectively.

The aggregation is a sum over all ion species and all ionic charge states,
not a density-weighted mean. Species-resolved [ion energy
flux](name:ion_energy_flux) and [ion charge-state energy
flux](name:ion_charge_state_energy_flux) provide contributions to this
total. Electron and neutral energy fluxes are excluded; the quantity is
neither a diffusion-only contribution nor a surface-integrated power.

The transport direction here is the outward magnetic-flux-surface normal,
not the cylindrical major-radius direction. In the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$
is vertical height; the direction of increasing $R$ is not generally normal
to a magnetic flux surface.

Sign convention: Positive when ion energy crosses the magnetic flux surface
outward toward the last closed flux surface.

items.name: accumulated_krypton_count
items.description:
Cumulative number of krypton atoms injected into the machine since plasma
breakdown, expressed as 36 equivalent electrons for each krypton atom.
items.documentation:
Cumulative number of krypton atoms injected into the machine since plasma
breakdown, expressed as 36 equivalent electrons for each krypton atom, is
the post-breakdown time integral of the krypton atom influx into the machine
with a fixed species multiplier. The multiplier is the krypton atomic number
used as an equivalent-electron counting convention.

The accumulated count at time $t$ is defined by

$$
N_{\mathrm{Kr,acc}}(t) = Z_{\mathrm{Kr}} \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{Kr,acc}}$ is the accumulated krypton count,
$Z_{\mathrm{Kr}}=36$ is the krypton atomic-number multiplier,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Kr}}$ is the krypton atom injection rate into the machine,
$t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time, $t$ is the evaluation time,
and $t'$ is the integration time.

The scope is krypton introduced after plasma breakdown; it excludes krypton
present before breakdown, non-krypton species, instantaneous injection rate,
and any plasma number density. The species population is not charge-state
resolved; if charge-state labels are used, krypton contributions are summed
over all charge states before applying the fixed multiplier.

The equivalent-electron convention means this quantity equals 36 times the
unweighted accumulated krypton atom count. It follows the same
post-breakdown accumulated-species convention as [accumulated neon
count](name:accumulated_neon_count), [accumulated ammonia
count](name:accumulated_ammonia_count), and [accumulated helium-3 count due
to gas injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection). The
factor 36 is a counting convention and does not specify the ionization state
of the injected krypton.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Dimensionless volume-averaged deuterium abundance ratio is the quotient of
the volume-averaged deuterium ion number density and the volume-averaged
electron number density over the same plasma volume. The deuterium numerator
is charge-state-summed over positive atomic ion charge states and excludes
neutral or molecular deuterium.
items.documentation:
Dimensionless volume-averaged deuterium abundance ratio is the
electron-density-normalized abundance of deuterium ions in a specified
plasma volume. It is the quotient of the [volume-averaged deuterium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density) and the [volume-averaged
electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density) evaluated over that
same volume.

The ratio is defined by the quotient of volume averages:

$$
f_{D,V} = \frac{\langle n_D \rangle_V}{\langle n_e \rangle_V}
$$

where $f_{D,V}$ is this abundance ratio, $n_D$ is the [deuterium
density](name:deuterium_density), $n_e$ is the electron density, $\langle
n_D \rangle_V$ is the [volume-averaged deuterium
density](name:volume_averaged_deuterium_density), $\langle n_e \rangle_V$ is
the [volume-averaged electron
density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density), and the subscript $V$
denotes averaging over the common plasma volume.

The numerator is the volume average of deuterium ion number density summed
over all positive atomic ion charge states. It excludes neutral deuterium
atoms, molecular deuterium, and deuterium bound in non-ion populations. The
aggregation convention is a quotient of two volume-averaged densities, not
the volume average of the pointwise ratio $n_D/n_e$.

For non-negative number densities and positive $\langle n_e \rangle_V$,
$f_{D,V}$ is non-negative. It is not the fraction of deuterium among all
fuel nuclei and does not represent the absolute deuterium particle
inventory. It differs from the [volume-averaged deuterium-tritium abundance
ratio](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_deuterium_tritium_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density),
which uses the combined deuterium-tritium numerator, while this quantity
uses deuterium alone.

items.name: perpendicular_fast_ion_pressure
items.description:
Pressure of fast ions of a specified species is the gyrotropic stress
perpendicular to the local magnetic field, summed over all ionic charge
states.
items.documentation:
Pressure of fast ions of a specified species is the principal
field-perpendicular component of their gyrotropic pressure tensor, summed
over all ionic charge states. Together with the field-parallel component, it
characterizes the anisotropic stress of that suprathermal ion population.

The perpendicular pressure is defined by the transverse second central
velocity moment:

$$
p_{i,\mathrm{fast},\perp}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_q \int \frac{m_i w_\perp^2}{2}\,f_{i,q,\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{w})\,d^3w
$$

where $p_{i,\mathrm{fast},\perp}$ is the perpendicular fast-ion pressure,
$i$ labels the specified ion species, $q$ labels its ionic charge states,
$\mathbf{x}$ is position, $m_i$ is the ion mass, and $f_{i,q,\mathrm{fast}}$
is the fast-ion velocity distribution for species $i$ and charge state $q$.
The random velocity $\mathbf{w}$ is measured relative to the mean velocity
of the corresponding fast-ion charge-state population, and $d^3w$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The squared perpendicular random speed is
$w_\perp^2=|\mathbf{w}-(\mathbf{w}\cdot\hat{b})\hat{b}|^2$, where
$\hat{b}=\mathbf{B}/|\mathbf{B}|$ is the unit vector along the local
magnetic field $\mathbf{B}$. The factor one-half averages the two transverse
degrees of freedom.

This quantity includes only nonthermal ions of the specified species. Its
charge-state aggregation is a direct additive sum of the [perpendicular
fast-ion charge-state
pressures](name:perpendicular_fast_ion_charge_state_pressure), not a
density-weighted mean. It excludes thermal-ion pressure, electron pressure,
and directed bulk-flow stress; it is neither the parallel pressure component
nor the isotropic trace pressure.

This species-resolved component contributes to the [fast-ion pressure
tensor](name:fast_ion_pressure). Summing it over all ion species gives the
[perpendicular total fast-ion
pressure](name:perpendicular_total_fast_ion_pressure), which is distinct
from the single-species quantity defined here.

items.name: total_xenon_fraction
items.description:
Dimensionless abundance ratio of xenon ion number density, summed over
ionization states, to electron number density in the same plasma domain.
items.documentation:
The xenon fraction measures the abundance of charged xenon relative to the
electron population in a plasma domain. It is a dimensionless
part-to-reference ratio, not a xenon density or an effective charge.

The fraction is defined by:

$$
f_{\mathrm{Xe}} = \frac{n_{\mathrm{Xe}}}{n_e}
$$

where $f_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the xenon fraction, $n_{\mathrm{Xe}}$ is the
total xenon ion number density summed over all positive ionization states,
and $n_e$ is the electron number density.

The numerator and denominator refer to the same plasma domain and use the
same spatial aggregation convention. Neutral xenon atoms are excluded, and
the quantity is not restricted to an individual xenon ionization state. The
specific volume-averaged realization applies the averaging operation to both
densities before forming the ratio, as defined by
[volume_averaged_total_xenon_fraction](name:volume_averaged_total_xenon_fraction).

The underlying xenon density is the charge-state-summed quantity represented
by [xenon_density](name:xenon_density); the fraction differs from it by
normalization to the electron density. The corresponding volume-averaged
xenon density is
[volume_averaged_xenon_density](name:volume_averaged_xenon_density), which
supplies the numerator for the volume-averaged realization.

items.name: propane_source_rate
items.description:
Instantaneous propane (C3H8) injection rate into the plasma vessel,
converted from molecules to equivalent electrons using 26 electrons per
neutral molecule.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the instantaneous source rate of propane gas entering the
plasma vessel, expressed using the equivalent-electron convention. Each
neutral C3H8 molecule contributes the total electron count of its
constituent atoms.

The equivalent-electron source rate is defined by

$$
S_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)=26\,\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)
$$

where $S_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)$ is the equivalent-electron source rate,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)$ is the propane molecular injection rate in
molecules per second, $t$ is time, and 26 is the dimensionless electron
count per neutral molecule: three carbon atoms contribute 18 electrons and
eight hydrogen atoms contribute 8 electrons. This is an instantaneous rate,
distinct from the accumulated propane count, which is the time-integrated
equivalent-electron inventory.

items.name: toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency
items.description:
Signed angular rate of an ion species’ bulk motion about the symmetry axis,
equal to toroidal flow velocity divided by local major radius and
density-weighted over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
The toroidal ion rotation frequency is the signed angular rate of a
specified ion species’ bulk motion about the toroidal symmetry axis. It is
the toroidal rotation-rate component of [ion rotation
frequency](name:ion_rotation_frequency).

The defining relation is

$$
\Omega_{i\phi} = \frac{v_{i\phi}}{R} = \frac{\sum_q n_{iq}\Omega_{iq\phi}}{\sum_q n_{iq}}
$$

where $i$ labels the selected ion species, $q$ labels its ionic charge
states, $\Omega_{i\phi}$ is the species’ toroidal angular rotation rate,
$v_{i\phi}$ is its toroidal bulk-flow velocity, and $R$ is the local major
radius. The quantity $n_{iq}$ is the number density of charge state $q$, and
$\Omega_{iq\phi}$ is its [toroidal ion charge-state rotation
frequency](name:toroidal_ion_charge_state_rotation_frequency). The toroidal
direction is the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $Z$ is vertical height.

This is a local quantity in a poloidal cross-section; no flux-surface
averaging or uniform rotation on a flux surface is implied. It is the
density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states of one species, not a sum
of their angular rates or an average over different ion species. With only
one populated charge state, it equals that charge state’s toroidal rotation
frequency. It describes collective bulk rotation rather than individual
gyrocenter transit or precession.

Sign convention: Positive when the ion species’ bulk toroidal flow is in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_momentum_flux
items.description:
Poloidal neutral momentum flux is linear momentum transported per unit area
and time in the local poloidal direction by the represented neutral
population.
items.documentation:
Poloidal neutral momentum flux is the local rate per unit area at which a
represented neutral population transports linear [momentum](name:momentum)
in the poloidal direction. The poloidal qualifier specifies the transport
direction, not an additional choice of transported momentum component.

As a directional component of [neutral momentum
flux](name:neutral_momentum_flux), it satisfies:

$$
\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}} = \boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0 \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol e}_{\mathrm{p}}
$$

where $\Gamma_{0,\mathrm{p}}$ is this poloidal flux, $\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_0$
is the neutral flux vector for the transported momentum component under
consideration, and $\hat{\boldsymbol e}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the local poloidal
unit tangent toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$. The subscripts $0$
and $\mathrm{p}$ identify the neutral population and poloidal direction,
respectively. The tangent lies along a magnetic-flux-surface contour in a
constant-$\phi$ plane of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame,
where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical
height.

For a represented neutral species, contributions from its internal states
are summed; the [poloidal neutral-state momentum
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_state_momentum_flux) instead retains resolution
of a specified neutral state. Charged-particle contributions are excluded.
The flux includes convective and thermal-pressure contributions and is not
restricted to diffusive transport.

Unlike the [poloidal neutral particle
flux](name:poloidal_neutral_particle_flux), which counts transported
particles, this quantity accounts for transported momentum. It is a local
directional projection, not a surface-integrated transport rate.

Sign convention: Positive when the momentum-flux vector has a component
toward increasing poloidal angle $\theta$.

items.name: radial_ion_momentum_source
items.description:
Signed local rate of ion linear-momentum transfer per unit volume in the
major-radius direction, summed over all ionic charge states of a specified
species.
items.documentation:
The radial ion momentum source is the local rate of transfer of linear
[momentum](name:momentum) to a specified ion species per unit volume,
projected along the major-radius direction. It includes contributions summed
over all ionic charge states of that species.

The projection and charge-state aggregation are defined by:

$$
S_{i,R} = \mathbf{S}_i \cdot \hat{R} = \sum_q \mathbf{S}_{i,q} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $S_{i,R}$ is the radial source component, $\mathbf{S}_i$ is the [ion
momentum source](name:ion_momentum_source) vector for species $i$,
$\mathbf{S}_{i,q}$ is its contribution from ionic charge state $q$, and $q$
denotes the ionic charge number. The sum covers all ionic charge states of
species $i$. The unit vector $\hat{R}$ points toward increasing major radius
$R$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is
the toroidal angle and $Z$ is vertical height.

This quantity is species-specific rather than summed over different ion
species; it excludes electron and neutral-particle contributions. The
major-radius direction is not generally normal to a magnetic flux surface.
This is a local source density, not momentum density or a [momentum
flux](name:momentum_flux) through a surface. The declared unit is
inconsistent with this volumetric momentum-transfer-rate definition.

Sign convention: Positive when the momentum transferred to the ion species
has a component toward increasing $R$, away from the toroidal symmetry axis.

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power
items.description:
Power transferred from a coherent electromagnetic wave to the bulk thermal
ions of a specified charge state, integrated over the plasma volume.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the volume-integrated power absorbed by the bulk thermal
ion population in a specified charge state from a coherent electromagnetic
wave. It is the thermal component of ion charge-state power and excludes
nonthermal ions and collisional energy exchange between plasma populations.

The total absorbed power is defined by

$$
P_{\mathrm{th},q} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{abs},\mathrm{th},q}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{th},q}$ is the thermal-ion power for charge state $q$,
$p_{\mathrm{abs},\mathrm{th},q}$ is the corresponding local coherent-wave
power-transfer density, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is the plasma volume. The
total includes all toroidal Fourier modes; [per-toroidal-mode thermal ion
charge-state power](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power)
resolves the same quantity by mode. It contributes to the broader [ion
absorbed wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power) and is a
charge-state-resolved component of ion charge-state power.

items.name: toroidal_fast_particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force
items.description:
Volume-integrated toroidal angular-momentum transfer to fast particles from
the Lorentz force associated with their radial current.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the total toroidal torque transferred to the fast-particle
population by the electromagnetic force associated with its radial current,
integrated over the plasma volume.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, with
$\hat{R}\times\hat{\phi}=\hat{Z}$, the radial-current contribution is
defined by

$$
\mathcal{T}_{\phi}=\int_V -R\,j_{R}^{\mathrm{fast}} B_Z\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $\mathcal{T}_{\phi}$ is the toroidal torque, $R$ is major radius,
$j_{R}^{\mathrm{fast}}$ is the radial current density carried by fast
particles, $B_Z$ is the vertical magnetic-field component, and $V$ is the
plasma volume. Equivalently, the integrand is
$R(\mathbf{j}^{\mathrm{fast}}\times\mathbf{B})_\phi$ when restricted to the
radial-current contribution.

This is a volume-integrated quantity and is distinct from the local
[toroidal torque density due to the j-cross-B
force](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force) and from
collisional torque transfer to fast particles [toroidal fast torque due to
collisions](name:toroidal_fast_torque_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when the resulting torque points in the direction
of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: flux_surface_averaged_helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of helium-3 ions averaged over the plasma boundary, summed
over all helium-3 ion charge states and excluding neutral helium-3.
items.documentation:
Number density of helium 3

The flux-surface average is defined by

$$
\langle n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}\rangle = \oint n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}\,dS/|\nabla\psi| \, / \, \oint dS/|\nabla\psi|
$$

where $\langle n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}\rangle$ is the averaged helium-3 ion
number density, $n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}$ is the local helium-3 ion number
density, $S$ is the plasma-boundary flux surface, $dS$ is its surface
element, and $\psi$ is the poloidal magnetic flux whose gradient magnitude
provides the averaging weight.

This quantity applies to helium-3 ions at the plasma boundary, is summed
over all helium-3 ion charge states, and excludes neutral helium-3. It is
not a local point value and does not include neutral atoms.

It is the flux-surface-averaged counterpart of the local [helium-3 ion
density at the plasma boundary](name:helium_3_density_at_plasma_boundary),
replacing the pointwise value with an
inverse-poloidal-flux-gradient-weighted surface mean. It differs from the
[volume-averaged helium-3 density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density),
which averages over the confined plasma volume rather than over the
plasma-boundary surface.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

Related quantities:
[flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_helium_4_density_at_plasma_boundary).

items.name: parallel_electron_particle_flux
items.description:
Parallel electron particle flux is the net electron crossing rate per unit
area perpendicular to the local magnetic field, signed along that field.
items.documentation:
Parallel electron particle flux is the signed net number flow of electrons
along the local magnetic field per unit area perpendicular to that field.
Electron motions in opposite directions contribute with opposite signs.

The defining velocity moment is

$$
\Gamma_{e,\parallel} = \int (\mathbf{v}\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}) f_e(\mathbf{v})\,d^3v = n_e u_{e,\parallel}
$$

where $\Gamma_{e,\parallel}$ is the parallel electron particle flux,
$\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity, $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit vector
along the local magnetic field, $f_e$ is the electron velocity distribution
normalized to the electron number density $n_e$, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The integral covers all electron velocities,
and $u_{e,\parallel}$ is the density-weighted bulk [parallel electron
velocity](name:parallel_electron_velocity).

This quantity is local, not an area-integrated particle rate or a one-way
incident flux. Its reference area is perpendicular to the magnetic field,
rather than the actual area of an inclined material surface. No thermal or
nonthermal population restriction is implied.

It specializes [electron particle flux](name:electron_particle_flux) by
choosing the local magnetic-field direction as the surface normal. Unlike
[parallel electron energy flux](name:parallel_electron_energy_flux), it
counts transported electrons without weighting them by their energy or
electric charge.

Sign convention: Positive when the net electron number flow is along the
local magnetic field.

items.name: x_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
X component of the neutron-detector direction unit vector is the direction
cosine along the x axis of the right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame, from
a field-of-view voxel center toward the detector center. It is a component
of a normalized pointing direction, not a position coordinate.
items.documentation:
X component of the neutron-detector direction unit vector is the projection
of the normalized direction from a field-of-view voxel center to the
neutron-detector center onto the positive $\hat{x}$ axis. The component is
resolved in the right-handed Cartesian $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ basis
and is a direction cosine, not a Cartesian position coordinate.

The normalized pointing component is defined by

$$
d_x = \left(\frac{\mathbf r_{\rm det}-\mathbf r_{\rm vox}}{\left\lVert \mathbf r_{\rm det}-\mathbf r_{\rm vox}\right\rVert}\right)\cdot\hat{\mathbf x}
$$

where $d_x$ is the x component of the neutron-detector direction unit
vector, $\mathbf r_{\rm det}$ is the detector-center position, $\mathbf
r_{\rm vox}$ is the voxel-center position, and $\hat{\mathbf x}$ is the
positive x basis vector.

Together with the [y
component](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector) and [z
component](name:z_direction_unit_vector_of_neutron_detector), $d_x$
specifies the full normalized direction from the voxel center toward the
detector center; for nonzero separation the components satisfy
$d_x^2+d_y^2+d_z^2=1$.

items.name: alfven_frequency_imaginary_part
items.description:
Damping rate when negative or growth rate when positive, the imaginary part
of the complex shear Alfvén continuum frequency, for a single toroidal mode
number at a given radial position.
items.documentation:
The imaginary part of the complex shear Alfvén continuum frequency, $\gamma
= \operatorname{Im}(\omega_A)$, sets how fast a shear Alfvén perturbation
grows or decays at a given radial position for a chosen toroidal mode number
$n$. Together with the oscillation frequency
[alfven_frequency_real_part](name:alfven_frequency_real_part) it fixes the
full time dependence, which under the $e^{-i\omega_A t}$ convention evolves
as

$$
\delta f(t) \propto e^{\gamma t}\, e^{-i\omega_r t}
$$

so a positive $\gamma$ marks an unstable, growing response and a negative
$\gamma$ a linearly damped one. A linear MHD calculation resolves $\gamma$
as a function of minor radius and toroidal mode number. The continuum is
purely real in ideal MHD, and a finite $\gamma$ arises from resistive,
kinetic, or energetic-particle effects, the same drives that excite the
discrete Alfvén eigenmodes occupying the continuum gaps. The full complex
value is the [alfven_frequency](name:alfven_frequency).

Sign convention: Positive when the mode amplitude grows exponentially in
time under the $e^{-i\omega_A t}$ convention.

items.name: effective_charge_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Effective charge at the internal transport barrier is the local effective
ion charge of the plasma mixture evaluated at the internal transport
barrier, expressed as the electron-density-normalized second charge moment
over all ion populations.
items.documentation:
Effective charge at the internal transport barrier is the local effective
ion charge of the plasma mixture evaluated at the internal transport
barrier. It characterizes the charge-state composition of the ion population
at that locus through the second moment of ion charge number normalized by
electron density.

Using the local ion populations, it is defined by:

$$
Z_{\mathrm{eff,itb}} = \frac{\sum_s n_s Z_s^2}{n_e}
$$

where $Z_{\mathrm{eff,itb}}$ is the effective charge at the internal
transport barrier, $s$ labels each ion population present at that locus,
$n_s$ is the number density of ion population $s$, $Z_s$ is its ion charge
number, and $n_e$ is the electron number density at the same locus.

This quantity is local to the internal transport barrier and represents the
plasma ion mixture there. The summation includes all ion species and charge
states present at the locus; it is not a value at the pedestal top, limiter,
or divertor target, and it is not an average over the confined plasma
volume.

Under quasineutrality, $n_e = \sum_s n_s Z_s$, so higher-charge ion
populations contribute in proportion to $Z_s^2$ in the numerator. This local
quantity is distinct from [volume-averaged effective
charge](name:volume_averaged_effective_charge), which characterizes
effective charge after aggregation over the plasma volume.

items.name: vertical_velocity_at_current_center
items.description:
Vertical velocity of the plasma-current centroid, defined by the rate of
change of its vertical position.
items.documentation:
The vertical velocity at the current center is the kinematic velocity of the
centroid of the plasma current distribution, describing motion along the
vertical direction rather than a local fluid velocity sampled at that point.

$$
v_{Z,c}(t)=\frac{dZ_c(t)}{dt}
$$

where $Z_c$ is the vertical coordinate of the current center in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $t$ is time, and $v_{Z,c}$ is
the corresponding signed velocity. The position $Z_c$ is defined by the
[vertical coordinate of the current
center](name:vertical_coordinate_of_current_center).

This quantity describes motion of the current-density-weighted
plasma-current centroid and is distinct from the local [vertical plasma
velocity](name:vertical_plasma_velocity) evaluated at that location.

Sign convention: Positive when the current center moves toward increasing
$Z$.

items.name: cumulative_inside_flux_surface_electron_particle_source_rate
items.description:
Electron particle source rate inside a magnetic flux surface is the net
production or removal of free electrons integrated over the enclosed plasma
volume.
items.documentation:
Electron particle source rate inside a magnetic flux surface is the net
production or removal of free electrons integrated over the enclosed plasma
volume. It supplies the source contribution to the volume-integrated
electron particle-number balance.

The cumulative rate is defined by

$$
S_{e,\mathrm{inside}}(\psi)=\int_{V(\psi)} S_{e,\mathrm{vol}}\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $S_{e,\mathrm{inside}}$ is the enclosed electron particle source rate,
$S_{e,\mathrm{vol}}$ is the local net free-electron volumetric source rate,
$\psi$ labels the selected magnetic flux surface, $V(\psi)$ is the plasma
volume enclosed by that surface, and $\mathrm{d}V$ is a physical volume
element.

The integral combines local electron gains and losses throughout the
enclosed volume for the source contribution under consideration. No
thermal-population or orbit-class restriction is implied. This quantity is a
spatial integral, not a flux-surface average or a time-integrated electron
inventory; it is distinct from the electron transport flux through the
enclosing surface.

The [cumulative ion charge-state source
rate](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_ion_charge_state_source_rate) uses
the same enclosed-volume integration for particles in a specified ion charge
state rather than for free electrons.

Sign convention: Positive when free-electron production exceeds removal
within the enclosed plasma volume.

items.name: poloidal_vector_potential
items.description:
Magnetic vector-potential quantity given by the signed projection of the
electromagnetic vector potential onto the local poloidal direction tangent
to increasing poloidal angle in the poloidal cross-section of the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is
toroidal angle, and Z is vertical height.
items.documentation:
The poloidal component of the magnetic vector potential is the signed
projection of the electromagnetic vector potential onto the local poloidal
direction in the poloidal cross-section of the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The local poloidal unit vector is tangent to increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$; $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ increases toroidally, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The component is defined by the scalar projection of the vector potential
onto the poloidal unit direction:

$$
A_\theta = \mathbf{A}\cdot\hat{e}_\theta
$$

where $A_\theta$ is the poloidal vector potential, $\mathbf{A}$ is the
magnetic vector-potential field, and $\hat{e}_\theta$ is the local unit
vector tangent to increasing $\theta$ in the $R$-$Z$ plane.

This quantity is a component of the gage-dependent vector potential, not a
component of the magnetic field. The associated magnetic-field vector
satisfies $\mathbf{B}=\nabla\times\mathbf{A}$ after a gage is fixed, and
replacing $\mathbf{A}$ by $\mathbf{A}+\nabla\chi$ leaves $\mathbf{B}$
unchanged. Related directional variants include the [radial vector
potential](name:radial_vector_potential), [poloidal magnetic vector
potential](name:poloidal_magnetic_vector_potential), [radial magnetic vector
potential](name:radial_magnetic_vector_potential), and [vertical magnetic
vector potential](name:vertical_magnetic_vector_potential).

Sign convention: Positive when the gage-fixed vector potential has a
component along $\hat{e}_\theta$, the local direction tangent to increasing
poloidal angle $\theta$ at fixed $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: beryllium_density_at_pedestal_top
items.description:
Local number density of ionized beryllium at the top of the H-mode edge
pedestal, summed over all beryllium ion charge states and excluding neutral
beryllium.
items.documentation:
Beryllium-ion number density at the top of the H-mode edge pedestal
represents the local concentration of ionized beryllium at the pedestal-top
location.

The total beryllium-ion density is defined by

$$
n_{\mathrm{Be}} = \sum_{q=1}^{4} n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Be}}$ is the total beryllium-ion number density,
$n_{\mathrm{Be}^{q+}}$ is the number density of beryllium ions with charge
state $q+$, and $q$ is the positive integer charge state from one through
four.

The quantity is evaluated locally at the pedestal top, whose position is
defined by the [normalized poloidal flux coordinate of the
pedestal](name:normalized_poloidal_flux_coordinate_of_pedestal). It applies
to ionized beryllium only and is summed over all included beryllium ion
charge states; neutral beryllium is excluded, and individual charge-state
densities are not reported separately.

This is the pedestal-top specialization of [beryllium
density](name:beryllium_density). Its charge-state aggregation is the same
as for [beryllium density at the magnetic
axis](name:beryllium_density_at_magnetic_axis), while the evaluation locus
differs.

items.name: initial_spun_twist_phase_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor
items.description:
Initial azimuthal phase specifying the starting orientation of the spun
fiber’s polarization axis along a fiber-optic current sensor.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the azimuthal orientation of the spun fiber’s polarization
axis at the starting end of a fiber-optic current sensor. It specifies the
initial state for polarization evolution along the sensing fiber.

$$
\theta_0 = \theta(s=0)
$$

where $\theta_0$ is the initial spun twist phase, $\theta(s)$ is the
polarization-axis azimuth at position $s$ along the fiber centerline, and
$s=0$ denotes the starting end.

This is an intrinsic fiber-frame orientation parameter, not the temporal
phase of an electromagnetic wave. The phase variation along the fiber is
characterized separately by the [twist period of the fiber-optic current
sensor](name:twist_period_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor); the zero and
positive angular sense follow the defined local polarization-frame
convention.

items.name: ratio_of_plasma_upper_bound_current_to_plasma_initial_current_due_to_disruption
items.description:
Fraction of the pre-disruptive plasma current represented by the upper
threshold used to define a custom linear current-quench decay interval.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the user-defined upper current threshold, expressed as a
fraction of the pre-disruptive plasma current during a disruption current
quench.

$$
X_2 = \frac{I_{\mathrm{upper}}}{I_{\mathrm{initial}}}
$$

where $X_2$ is the upper threshold fraction, $I_{\mathrm{upper}}$ is the
plasma current at that threshold, and $I_{\mathrm{initial}}$ is the
pre-disruptive plasma current.

The threshold is paired with a lower fraction $X_1$ to define a custom
linear decay interval, whose effective decay time is
$(t(X_2)-t(X_1))/(X_1-X_2)$; $t(X_j)$ is the time at which the plasma
current reaches fraction $X_j$ of its pre-disruptive value. This quantity is
a threshold fraction, not a decay time, unlike the [thermal energy decay
time due to disruption](name:thermal_energy_decay_time_due_to_disruption).

items.name: wavelength_of_detector_pixel
items.description:
Wavelength assigned to incoming photons at an X-ray crystal spectrometer
detector pixel, including Bragg dispersion and curvature-induced variation
across the detector face.
items.documentation:
The wavelength associated with a detector pixel is the vacuum spectral
coordinate of incoming photons whose Bragg-dispersed rays reach that pixel.

The pixel-specific wavelength follows Bragg's law:

$$
\lambda_{\rm pix}=2d\sin\theta_{\rm pix}
$$

where $\lambda_{\rm pix}$ is the vacuum wavelength assigned to the incoming
photons at the pixel, $d$ is the crystal lattice-plane spacing, and
$\theta_{\rm pix}$ is the Bragg angle for rays reaching that pixel.

This quantity is a per-pixel spectral assignment for an X-ray crystal
spectrometer. It primarily varies along the dispersive detector direction
and also varies along the perpendicular detector-face direction because the
constant-wavelength surfaces have elliptical curvature. It is not a single
wavelength averaged over the detector face or over a wavelength band, and it
does not denote the crystal's wavelength independently of a pixel.

It is a detector-pixel specialization of vacuum electromagnetic wavelength.
Unlike [energy_of_detector_pixel](name:energy_of_detector_pixel), which uses
photon energy as the spectral coordinate, this quantity uses wavelength for
the same pixel-specific incoming-photon assignment.

items.name: perpendicular_fast_particle_energy
items.description:
Perpendicular fast-particle energy is the part of the suprathermal particle
kinetic energy associated with motion perpendicular to the local magnetic
field, integrated over the plasma volume.
items.documentation:
Perpendicular fast-particle energy is the part of the kinetic energy of the
suprathermal particle population associated with motion perpendicular to the
local magnetic field. It complements [parallel fast-particle
energy](name:parallel_fast_particle_energy) within the total [fast-particle
energy](name:fast_particle_energy).

It is defined by

$$
W_{\perp,\mathrm{fast}} = \int_{\mathcal{V}} \int \frac{1}{2} m v_\perp^2 f_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v\,d^3r
$$

where $\mathcal{V}$ is the plasma volume,
$f_{\mathrm{fast}}(\mathbf{r},\mathbf{v})$ is the fast-particle phase-space
distribution, $m$ is particle mass, and $v_\perp$ is the speed component
perpendicular to the local magnetic field. For a gyrotropic distribution,
the corresponding energy density is the perpendicular pressure, so the
quantity equals the volume integral of [perpendicular fast-particle
pressure](name:perpendicular_fast_particle_pressure), summed over the
included fast-particle species.

items.name: parallel_neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity
items.description:
Signed effective velocity along the local magnetic field relating the
thermal energy-density factor to the convective energy flux of one neutral
species in a specified internal state.
items.documentation:
Parallel neutral internal-state energy convection velocity is the
field-aligned component of the effective velocity coefficient governing
convective thermal-energy transport. It specializes [energy convection
velocity](name:energy_convection_velocity) to one neutral species in one
specified internal state.

Its defining energy-flux relation is:

$$
Q_{0,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}} = \mathcal{W}_{0,a}\,v_{0,a,W,\parallel}
$$

where $Q_{0,a,\parallel}^{\mathrm{conv}}$ is the parallel convective
thermal-energy flux, $\mathcal{W}_{0,a}$ is the transported thermal
energy-density factor, and $v_{0,a,W,\parallel}$ is the effective parallel
energy-convection velocity. The subscript $0$ identifies the neutral
population, $a$ identifies its specified internal state, $W$ denotes the
energy transport channel, and $\parallel$ denotes projection along the local
magnetic field.

This coefficient applies separately to the specified species and internal
state; it is neither summed nor averaged over species or internal states. It
describes the convective contribution, not gradient-driven energy diffusion,
and need not equal the [bulk neutral internal-state
velocity](name:bulk_neutral_internal_state_velocity).

It is the projection of the [neutral internal-state energy convection
velocity](name:neutral_internal_state_energy_convection_velocity):
$v_{0,a,W,\parallel}=\mathbf{v}_{0,a,W}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}$, where
$\mathbf{v}_{0,a,W}$ is that parent vector coefficient and $\hat{\mathbf b}$
is the unit vector along the local magnetic field. This projection requires
a nonzero local magnetic field and does not imply that neutral particles are
magnetically confined.

Sign convention: Positive when the effective energy-convection velocity
points along the local magnetic field.

items.name: electron_density_at_launching_position
items.description:
Electron number density at the wave-launching position is the local
free-electron count per unit volume where an injected electromagnetic wave
first contacts the edge plasma.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local free-electron number density at the geometric
launching position, such as a wave launcher aperture or waveguide mouth
where an injected electromagnetic wave first contacts the edge plasma. It is
the electron-specific component of number density at the launching position.

The density is defined from the electron velocity-distribution function by

$$
n_e(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{launch}})=\int f_e(\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{launch}},\mathbf{v})\,d^3\mathbf{v}
$$

where $n_e$ is electron number density, $\mathbf{x}_{\mathrm{launch}}$ is
the launching position, $f_e$ is the electron velocity-distribution
function, and $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity.

This is a local value for free electrons at the launching position, not a
density summed over plasma species, a flux-surface average, or a wave-power
quantity. It is distinct from [electron number density at the plasma
boundary](name:electron_density_at_plasma_boundary), which is evaluated at
the last closed flux surface.

items.name: helium_4_density_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Particle number density of helium-4 ions at the internal transport barrier,
the flux-surface location where locally reduced cross-field turbulent
transport permits steep radial helium-4 density gradients to form.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of helium-4 ions at the internal transport barrier
is the local, isotope-resolved helium-ion density on the flux surface
selected as the barrier reference location. Helium-4 ($^4\mathrm{He}$, mass
number $A = 4$) is the stable alpha-particle product of deuterium-tritium
fusion and may also be present from helium fueling or wall recycling. The
internal transport barrier is a confined-plasma flux-surface region where
locally reduced cross-field transport permits steep radial gradients to
form.

The local density is the charge-state-summed zeroth velocity moment
evaluated at the ITB reference radius:

$$
n_{{}^4\mathrm{He},\mathrm{ITB}} = \sum_{q>0} \int f_{{}^4\mathrm{He}^{q+}}(\mathbf{v}, \rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm,ITB}})\, d^3v
$$

where $q$ indexes positive ion charge states, $f_{{}^4\mathrm{He}^{q+}}$ is
the phase-space distribution function of helium-4 ions with charge state
$q+$, $\mathbf{v}$ is particle velocity, the integral is over velocity
space, and $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm,ITB}}$ is the normalized toroidal-flux
radius of the ITB reference flux surface.

Unless a charge state is specified separately, this species-level density is
summed over all helium-4 ion charge states and excludes neutral helium-4
atoms; in hot core plasma the ionic population is commonly dominated by
fully stripped $\mathrm{He}^{2+}$. This is the helium-4 member of
[density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
and a species-specific instance of
ion_density_at_internal_transport_barrier; it is distinct from
[helium_3_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:helium_3_density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
by isotope mass and from
[electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier](name:electron_density_at_internal_transport_barrier)
by particle species.

items.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector
items.description:
Signed second local-tangential coordinate of a neutral beam injector outline
vertex, measured in the injector-local frame and paired with the first
coordinate to locate that vertex.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed position of an outline vertex along the neutral
beam injector's second local tangential axis. It is paired with the [first
local-tangential
coordinate](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_neutral_beam_injector)
to locate the same vertex in the injector-local frame.

The coordinate is defined by:

$$
x_2 = (\mathbf{r}_v-\mathbf{r}_0)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2
$$

where $x_2$ is this coordinate, $\mathbf{r}_v$ is the vertex position,
$\mathbf{r}_0$ is the local origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2$ is the second
local tangential unit vector. The local orthonormal basis
$(\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2,\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3)$ is
right-handed; $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3$ is the plasma-facing normal, and
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The coordinate applies to outline vertices associated with the neutral beam
injector and is distinct from the first local-tangential coordinate and from
global cylindrical coordinates.

Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement has a positive
projection along
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_2=\hat{\mathbf{e}}_3\times\hat{\mathbf{e}}_1$ from the
local origin.

items.name: argon_prefill_count
items.description:
Argon prefill count is the total amount of neutral argon (Ar) introduced
before plasma breakdown, expressed as an equivalent-electron count with 18
per atom.
items.documentation:
Argon prefill count is the total amount of neutral argon (Ar) introduced
during the prefill phase before plasma breakdown, expressed as an
equivalent-electron count. Each neutral argon atom contributes 18 equivalent
electrons.

The equivalent-electron count is obtained by accumulating injected argon
atoms over the prefill interval and weighting them by the argon atomic
number:

$$
N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} N_{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}} = Z_{\mathrm{Ar}} \int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t)\,dt = 18\int_{t_0}^{t_{\mathrm{bd}}} \dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}(t)\,dt
$$

where $N_{e,\mathrm{eq}}^{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}}$ is the equivalent-electron
count, $N_{\mathrm{Ar,prefill}}$ is the accumulated neutral-argon atom
count, $Z_{\mathrm{Ar}}=18$ is the argon atomic number,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{Ar}}$ is the argon atom injection rate, $t_0$ is the
prefill start time, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the plasma-breakdown time.

This quantity includes only argon introduced before breakdown and excludes
wall recycling, neutral-beam or pellet fueling, later gas injection, and
retained or ionized inventory. It is the argon-specific component of
[prefill count](name:prefill_count) and follows the isotope-resolved
convention used for tritium prefill count.

items.name: safety_factor
items.description:
Safety factor is the signed number of toroidal turns made by a magnetic
field line per complete poloidal circuit on a toroidal magnetic flux
surface.
items.documentation:
Safety factor is the signed toroidal-to-poloidal winding ratio of magnetic
field lines on a toroidal magnetic flux surface. It characterizes magnetic
geometry without selecting a particular surface or plasma region.

In axisymmetry, or using straight-field-line flux coordinates
$(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, the defining relation is

$$
q = \frac{1}{2\pi}\oint \frac{\mathbf{B}\cdot\nabla\phi}{\mathbf{B}\cdot\nabla\theta}\,d\theta
$$

where $q$ is the safety factor, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $\nabla$
is the spatial gradient operator, $\rho$ labels magnetic flux surfaces,
$\theta$ is the poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is the toroidal angle. The
integral follows a magnetic field line through one complete poloidal
circuit. The toroidal angle belongs to the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height;
$\phi$ increases counter-clockwise when viewed from above.

The quantity describes winding on an individual magnetic surface, not a
volume average or a sum over surfaces. It applies to closed magnetic
surfaces in both core and edge regions. On open scrape-off-layer field
lines, a complete poloidal circuit need not exist, so any extension of this
definition requires an additional convention.

The [magnetic-axis safety factor](name:safety_factor_at_magnetic_axis) and
[plasma-boundary safety factor](name:safety_factor_at_plasma_boundary) are
limiting values approached from neighboring closed surfaces; a separatrix
limit need not be finite. The [minimum safety
factor](name:minimum_safety_factor) instead selects the signed value on the
closed surface where the safety-factor magnitude is smallest, rather than
evaluating it at a prescribed locus.

Sign convention: Positive when the toroidal angle advance of a magnetic
field line is in the direction of increasing $\phi$ as the poloidal angle
$\theta$ increases.

items.name: center_of_mass_velocity_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Mass-density-weighted mean of all constituent species' diamagnetic drift
velocities, representing the diamagnetic contribution to plasma
center-of-mass motion.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local diamagnetic contribution to the plasma
center-of-mass velocity, formed as the mass-density-weighted mean of
constituent species' diamagnetic velocity contributions. It is this
contribution alone, not the complete plasma center-of-mass velocity.

The mass-density-weighted mean is defined by:

$$
\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm,dia}} = \frac{\sum_a \rho_a\,\mathbf{v}_{a,\mathrm{dia}}}{\sum_a \rho_a}
$$

where $\mathbf{V}_{\mathrm{cm,dia}}$ is the diamagnetic center-of-mass
velocity contribution, $a$ indexes the constituent species and charge-state
populations, $\rho_a$ is the mass density of population $a$, and
$\mathbf{v}_{a,\mathrm{dia}}$ is its diamagnetic velocity contribution.

The aggregation is over all constituent plasma species at the same location,
not a spatial average or a charge-weighted electric current. For an
intensive species velocity resolved by charge state, the charge-state
aggregation is a density-weighted mean over all charge states. This quantity
is the diamagnetic contribution to the [center-of-mass
velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity); other velocity contributions are
excluded.

items.name: source_due_to_diamagnetic_drift
items.description:
Area-normalized vector source term due to diamagnetic drift is the
pressure-gradient-driven contribution to a transport momentum balance. It
represents directional transfer of linear momentum associated with
diamagnetic drift, not the total source from all mechanisms.
items.documentation:
Area-normalized vector source term due to diamagnetic drift is the part of a
transport momentum-balance source vector produced by diamagnetic drift in a
magnetized plasma. The diamagnetic-drift contribution is the
pressure-gradient-driven part of the directional transfer of linear
momentum, separated from other transport mechanisms.

When represented from a local source density over a balance region, the
area-normalized source is defined by

$$
\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{dia}} = \frac{1}{A}\int_V \mathbf{s}_{\mathrm{dia}}\,dV
$$

where $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the area-normalized vector source term
due to diamagnetic drift, $\mathbf{s}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the local vector
source density due to diamagnetic drift, $V$ is the balance region, $dV$ is
the volume element, $A$ is the surface area used for the normalization, and
the subscript $\mathrm{dia}$ denotes the diamagnetic-drift contribution.

The scope is restricted to the diamagnetic-drift part of the source, meaning
the contribution associated with pressure gradients in the charged plasma
population and balance region specified by the more specific quantity. At
this parent level no species, charge state, momentum projection, or vector
component is selected; the aggregation convention is integration over the
balance region followed by normalization by the associated surface area.

This quantity does not denote the total source from all mechanisms, a volume
average, or a scalar particle, heat, or energy source. It also excludes
source terms from other drift, collisional, neutral, wave, or externally
applied mechanisms except insofar as they are part of the diamagnetic-drift
contribution itself.

The [momentum source due to diamagnetic
drift](name:momentum_source_due_to_diamagnetic_drift) is the momentum-source
specialization of this parent: it keeps the same diamagnetic-drift mechanism
and area normalization while specifying the balanced transferred quantity as
projected linear momentum.

Sign convention: Positive when a component of $\mathbf{S}_{\mathrm{dia}}$
transfers linear momentum in the positive direction of the basis vector onto
which that component is projected.

items.name: toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Signed toroidal component of the bulk-flow velocity of helium-4 ions
evaluated on the last closed magnetic flux surface.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local bulk-flow velocity component of helium-4 ions at
the plasma boundary, identified with the last closed magnetic flux surface.
It is not a flux-surface average.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, the component is
defined by

$$
v_\phi = \mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}4}} \cdot \hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}
$$

where $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}4}}$ is the bulk-flow velocity of the
helium-4 ion population and $\hat{\boldsymbol{\phi}}$ is the unit vector in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle. The boundary-local value is
distinct from the [toroidal helium-4 velocity at the magnetic
axis](name:toroidal_helium_4_velocity_at_magnetic_axis) and from a
flux-surface-averaged helium velocity.

items.name: wavelength_of_spectral_line
items.description:
Wavelength of a spectral line in vacuum in the emitter's rest frame,
providing the unshifted reference before Doppler and motional Stark shifts.
items.documentation:
Wavelength of spectral line

The reference wavelength satisfies:

$$
\lambda = \frac{c}{\nu_0}
$$

where $\lambda$ is the unshifted vacuum [wavelength], $c$ is the speed of
light in vacuum, and $\nu_0$ is the corresponding rest-frame transition
frequency before motional Stark shifts.

This line-specific value provides the reference for [neutral-beam Doppler
wavelength
displacements](name:difference_of_neutral_beam_doppler_wavelength_and_reference_wavelength_of_spectral_line)
and [motional Stark wavelength
displacements](name:difference_of_fast_neutral_beam_motional_stark_wavelength_and_fast_neutral_beam_reference_wavelength_of_spectral_line);
neither displacement is included in the reference wavelength itself.

Unlike the [wavelength assigned to a detector
pixel](name:wavelength_of_detector_pixel), this quantity characterizes the
transition rather than the spectral coordinate selected by the optical
response. It is not a line width or an average over different spectral
lines.

items.name: spectral_efficiency_of_neutron_detector
items.description:
Energy-dependent probability that an incident neutron within a specified
energy band is recorded as an accepted count by the neutron detector.
items.documentation:
Neutron spectral efficiency is the conditional probability that an incident
neutron in the detector's assigned energy interval produces an accepted
detector count.

For incident neutron energy $E$, the efficiency is defined by

$$
\epsilon(E) = \frac{N_{\mathrm{recorded}}(E)}{N_{\mathrm{incident}}(E)}
$$

where $\epsilon(E)$ is the detection probability, $N_{\mathrm{recorded}}(E)$
is the number of accepted counts produced by neutrons in a narrow interval
around energy $E$, and $N_{\mathrm{incident}}(E)$ is the number of neutrons
impacting the detector in that interval.

This quantity applies only to the neutron detector and its specified
incident-energy band. It is a conditional probability for individual
incident neutrons, not a sum over neutron populations or energy bands, and
it excludes the incident neutron flux itself and detector signals rejected
by the counting criterion.

The energy domain is bounded by the detector-band limits, including the
[maximum neutron energy of the neutron
detector](name:neutron_maximum_energy_of_neutron_detector). It is the
neutron counterpart of [spectral efficiency of a hard X-ray
detector](name:spectral_efficiency_of_hard_xray_detector), which describes
the analogous counting probability for photons rather than neutrons.

items.name: thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density
items.description:
Volumetric rate of coherent-wave power absorbed by bulk thermal ions of a
selected species and charge state, or a selected bundle of charge states. It
is represented as a local value or as an average over a magnetic flux
surface.
items.documentation:
Thermal ion charge-state power density is the volumetric rate of
coherent-wave power absorbed by bulk thermal ions associated with a selected
ion species and charge state, or a selected bundle of charge states. It can
be expressed as a local value or as an average over a magnetic flux surface.

The local absorbed-power density is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{th},a} = \frac{dP_{\mathrm{abs,th},a}}{dV}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{th},a}$ is the thermal ion charge-state power density,
$P_{\mathrm{abs,th},a}$ is the coherent-wave power absorbed by the selected
thermal-ion population, $V$ is physical volume, the subscript $\mathrm{th}$
identifies the bulk thermal-ion population, and $a$ identifies the selected
species and charge state or charge-state bundle.

The recipient population is bulk thermal ions of the selected species. For a
charge-state bundle, the value is summed over its constituent charge states;
it is not summed over other charge states or species. The local value
resolves spatial deposition, while the flux-surface-averaged value averages
that deposition over a magnetic flux surface without changing the recipient
population or energy-transfer channel.

This quantity excludes absorption by nonthermal fast ions, described by
[fast-ion charge-state power
density](name:fast_ion_charge_state_power_density). It is the coherent-wave
absorption contribution to [ion charge-state power
density](name:ion_charge_state_power_density), which is the net
energy-transfer rate across the included processes. Collisional energy
transfer to thermal ions is distinct from wave absorption and is described
by [thermal-ion charge-state power density due to
collisions](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

The [toroidal-mode-resolved
counterpart](name:per_toroidal_mode_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density)
resolves this deposition by toroidal Fourier harmonic. Integrating the
flux-surface-averaged density over the volume enclosed by a magnetic flux
surface gives the [thermal ion charge-state power at the enclosed flux
surface](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_power_at_inside_flux_surface).

items.name: first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror
items.description:
First local tangential coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror is its signed displacement from the
mirror-local origin along the first local tangential direction. That
direction is the more horizontally directed in-plane mirror tangent oriented
toward increasing toroidal angle φ in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical
height.
items.documentation:
First local tangential coordinate of a point on the closed outline of an
electron-cyclotron launcher mirror is the signed scalar projection of the
point displacement from the mirror-local origin onto the mirror's first
local tangential axis. The mirror-local orthonormal triad $(\hat{\mathbf
t}_1, \hat{\mathbf t}_2, \hat{\mathbf n})$ has $\hat{\mathbf t}_1$ and
$\hat{\mathbf t}_2$ tangent to the mirror outline plane and $\hat{\mathbf
n}$ as the plasma-facing normal. The first local tangential axis
$\hat{\mathbf t}_1$ is the more horizontally directed in-plane tangent,
oriented toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

The coordinate is defined by the Euclidean projection of the outline-point
position relative to the mirror-local origin onto the first local tangential
unit vector:

$$
\xi_1 = (\mathbf r - \mathbf r_0) \cdot \hat{\mathbf t}_1
$$

where $\xi_1$ is the first local tangential coordinate of the mirror outline
point, $\mathbf r$ is the position vector of the outline point, $\mathbf
r_0$ is the mirror-local origin, and $\hat{\mathbf t}_1$ is the first local
tangential unit vector.

This coordinate is paired with the [second local tangential coordinate of
the electron-cyclotron launcher
mirror](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror),
which uses $\hat{\mathbf t}_2$ in the same mirror-local tangential plane.
The second local tangential direction is fixed by $\hat{\mathbf t}_2 =
\hat{\mathbf n} \times \hat{\mathbf t}_1$, so $\hat{\mathbf t}_1 \times
\hat{\mathbf t}_2 = \hat{\mathbf n}$. This local coordinate is distinct from
locating the mirror in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame
through quantities such as the radial centroid of the electron-cyclotron
launcher mirror and the [vertical coordinate of the electron-cyclotron
launcher
mirror](name:vertical_coordinate_of_electron_cyclotron_launcher_mirror).

Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the mirror-local origin
to the outline point has a component in the direction of $\hat{\mathbf
t}_1$.

items.name: pfirsch_schlueter_current_density
items.description:
Pfirsch-Schlueter current density is the vector flux density of conventional
electric charge, equal to electric current per unit area normal to the flow,
for the neoclassical return current that restores current continuity when
the pressure-gradient diamagnetic current is divergent in toroidal magnetic
geometry. It denotes the full vector before scalar projection.
items.documentation:
Pfirsch-Schlueter current density $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the vector
density of conventional electric charge flux associated with the
neoclassical return current in toroidal magnetic confinement geometry. It
restores local current continuity when the pressure-gradient
diamagnetic_current_density has finite divergence caused by magnetic-field
inhomogeneity. It is a contribution to
[current_density](name:current_density) and varies around a magnetic flux
surface while remaining predominantly aligned with the magnetic field.

The defining continuity relation for the pressure-gradient part of the
current is:

$$
\nabla\cdot\left(\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}+\frac{\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p}{B^2}\right)=0
$$

where $\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}$ is the Pfirsch-Schlueter current density,
$\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic field, $B=|\mathbf{B}|$, and $p$ is the total
scalar plasma pressure. The term $\mathbf{B}\times\nabla p/B^2$ is the
pressure-gradient diamagnetic current density, so the equation states that
the Pfirsch-Schlueter return current closes its divergence. In the
field-aligned neoclassical representation, the vector is reconstructed from
the parallel amplitude as
$\mathbf{J}_{\mathrm{PS}}=j_{\parallel,\mathrm{PS}}\mathbf{b}$ with
$\mathbf{b}=\mathbf{B}/B$; scalar component names are projections of this
vector.

This quantity excludes bootstrap_current_density, Ohmic current density,
externally driven current density, and the diamagnetic current density
itself, although these may enter the total current balance. The generic name
denotes the unprojected vector; related projections include
[parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:parallel_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density)
along $\mathbf{b}$,
[poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:poloidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density)
along increasing $\theta$ in flux coordinates $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$, where
$\rho$ labels flux surfaces, $\theta$ is poloidal angle, and $\phi$ is
toroidal angle, and
[radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:radial_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density),
[toroidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:toroidal_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density),
and
[vertical_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density](name:vertical_pfirsch_schlueter_current_density)
along $\hat{R}$, $\hat{\phi}$, and $\hat{Z}$ in the right-handed cylindrical
