$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and
$Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: parallel_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part
items.description:
Signed imaginary quadrature of a wave electric-field phasor projected along
the local equilibrium magnetic field, relative to a specified phase
reference.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the signed imaginary quadrature of the wave [electric
field](name:electric_field) phasor projected along the local equilibrium
magnetic field. It describes the field-aligned contribution to the complex
wave polarization at each point along a propagation path.

The defining projection and quadrature extraction are

$$
E_{\parallel,I}=\operatorname{Im}\!\left(\widetilde E_\parallel\right)=\operatorname{Im}\!\left(\widetilde{\mathbf E}\cdot\hat{\mathbf b}\right).
$$

Here $E_{\parallel,I}$ is the signed imaginary quadrature, $\widetilde
E_\parallel$ is the [parallel wave electric-field
phasor](name:parallel_wave_electric_field), $\widetilde{\mathbf E}$ is the
wave electric-field phasor, and $\operatorname{Im}$ extracts its imaginary
coefficient. The unit vector $\hat{\mathbf b}=\mathbf B_0/|\mathbf B_0|$
points along the local equilibrium magnetic field $\mathbf B_0$.

This is a local field contribution, not a path integral or average. Parallel
refers to the equilibrium magnetic-field direction, not necessarily the
propagation direction. Unlike the [left-hand circularly polarized imaginary
quadrature](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part),
it does not resolve transverse circular polarization.

Together with the [parallel wave electric-field real
part](name:parallel_wave_electric_field_real_part), this quadrature
determines the full parallel phasor. It is neither the phasor magnitude nor
the instantaneous physical field; its value depends on the chosen phase
reference and temporal Fourier convention.

Sign convention: Positive when the imaginary-quadrature projection points
along, rather than opposite to, the local equilibrium magnetic field, with
the phasor phase reference and temporal Fourier convention held fixed.

items.name: poloidal_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Signed projection onto an oriented local poloidal direction of an effective
E×B fluid drift assigned to one neutral species in a specified internal
state.
items.documentation:
The poloidal component of the [effective neutral internal-state E×B drift
velocity](name:effective_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift)
is its signed projection along a specified local poloidal direction. This
direction lies in a constant-toroidal-angle plane of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal
symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height. The
positive local poloidal orientation must be specified explicitly.

For the assigned ideal E×B drift, the defining projection is

$$
v^0_{E,\mathrm{p}} = \mathbf{v}^0_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}} = \frac{(\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B})\cdot\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}.
$$

Here $v^0_{E,\mathrm{p}}$ is the effective poloidal drift component for the
specified neutral internal state, $\mathbf{v}^0_E$ is its assigned ideal E×B
drift velocity, $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric field, $\mathbf{B}$ is
the local magnetic field, and $\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the unit
vector along the specified positive local poloidal direction. The
superscript $0$ labels the neutral population, and the subscript
$\mathrm{p}$ denotes the poloidal projection. The definition requires a
nonzero magnetic field.

This quantity applies locally to one specified internal state of one neutral
species in the edge plasma; it is neither summed nor averaged over internal
states or species. It denotes an effective fluid-velocity contribution, not
a direct charged-particle guiding-center drift of electrically neutral
particles. Other contributions to neutral motion are excluded. It is a
linear velocity component, not a poloidal angle or angular velocity.

Unlike the [parallel
component](name:parallel_neutral_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift),
which vanishes identically for the assigned ideal E×B drift, the poloidal
projection need not vanish: the local poloidal direction is not generally
aligned with the local magnetic field.

Sign convention: Positive when the assigned E×B velocity has a component
along the specified positive local poloidal direction
$\hat{\mathbf{e}}_{\mathrm{p}}$.

items.name: ion_charge_state_lower_bound_charge
items.description:
Lower-bound charge number is the smallest ionic charge number included in a
specified charge-state bundle of a single ion species.
items.documentation:
Lower-bound charge specifies the inclusive lower endpoint of the ionization
charge-number range represented by a charge-state bundle of one ion species.
It identifies the bundle's extent independently of the relative populations
of its constituent charge states.

The lower bound is defined by:

$$
Z_{\min} = \min_{Z \in \mathcal{B}} Z
$$

where $Z_{\min}$ is the lower-bound charge number and $\mathcal{B}$ is the
set of ionic charge numbers represented by the bundle. Each $Z$ is an ionic
charge number defined by $Z=q/e$, where $q$ is the net electric charge per
particle and $e$ is the positive elementary charge. This is [normalized
particle charge](name:normalized_particle_charge) with the reference charge
chosen as $e$.

Together with the [maximum charge
number](name:ion_state_maximum_charge_number), denoted $Z_{\max}$, the lower
bound delimits the included range through $Z_{\min}\leq Z\leq Z_{\max}$. A
single resolved charge state has $Z_{\min}=Z_{\max}$; for a neutral state,
both bounds are zero.

The lower bound is not a population-weighted [charge-number moment of the
bundle](name:ion_charge_state_charge_number), a sum over charge states, or
the [nuclear charge number](name:ion_atomic_number), which counts protons
rather than net ionic charge.

items.name: accumulated_propane_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Cumulative post-breakdown propane inventory delivered by gas injection,
expressed as 26 equivalent electrons for each neutral molecule.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative inventory of neutral propane
($\mathrm{C_3H_8}$) molecules delivered by gas injection after plasma
breakdown. It represents delivered propane inventory, not the number of free
electrons in the plasma or the ionization state of the propane.

For evaluation time $t$ after breakdown, the equivalent-electron count is
defined by:

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t) = 26N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t) = \int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t} 26\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t')\,dt'
$$

where $N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)$ is the accumulated equivalent-electron count,
$N_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t)$ is the cumulative number of propane molecules
delivered by time $t$, $\dot{N}_{\mathrm{C_3H_8}}(t')$ is the instantaneous
propane molecular delivery rate at integration time $t'$, $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$
is the plasma-breakdown time, and $t'$ is the integration variable. The
factor 26 is the total number of electrons in one neutral propane molecule:
three carbon atoms contribute six each and eight hydrogen atoms contribute
one each.

The scope is restricted to propane introduced by gas injection after
breakdown and includes all such molecules delivered up to the evaluation
time. It excludes prefill propane and does not represent inventory from
other gas species, free plasma-electron content, or an
ionization-state-resolved amount.

Unlike the [propane prefill count](name:propane_prefill_count), which covers
propane introduced before breakdown, this quantity covers the post-breakdown
interval. Unlike the [propane source rate](name:propane_source_rate), it is
cumulative rather than instantaneous.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_pellet_path
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic flux at a pellet-path point is the value of the
equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux function evaluated at the position of a
pellet along its injection trajectory. For an axisymmetric equilibrium it
depends only on the major-radius and vertical coordinates of that trajectory
point.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at a pellet-path point is the value of the
equilibrium [poloidal_magnetic_flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux) function
sampled at the location of a pellet along its injection trajectory. It
labels the magnetic flux surface threading that trajectory point and shares
the sign and normalization of the underlying equilibrium flux function.

The quantity is the equilibrium poloidal flux function evaluated at the
pellet position:

$$
\psi_p = \psi\!\left(R_p, Z_p\right)
$$

where $\psi(R, Z)$ is the axisymmetric equilibrium poloidal magnetic-flux
function in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, with $R$ the
major radius and $Z$ the vertical height, and $(R_p, Z_p)$ are the
major-radius and vertical coordinates of the pellet-path point. Because the
equilibrium is axisymmetric, $\psi$ is independent of the toroidal angle
$\phi$, so the toroidal location of the trajectory point does not enter this
value.

This is one scalar flux value associated with a single point on the pellet
trajectory; sampled at successive points or instants along the path it
traces the sequence of flux-surface labels crossed by the pellet. It differs
from
[poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_flux_surface),
which is the flux value attached to a specified magnetic flux surface
independent of any trajectory. It is not the toroidal magnetic flux, the
pellet trajectory geometry, or a derivative of the flux label with respect
to a flux coordinate.

Sign convention: Positive when the vertical magnetic field on the horizontal
disk that defines the equilibrium poloidal flux points in the $+Z$ direction
of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_sawtooth_mixing_radius
items.description:
Normalized toroidal-flux surface label evaluated at the sawtooth mixing
radius, marking the outer boundary of the plasma region homogenized during a
sawtooth crash.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the normalized toroidal magnetic-flux label of the magnetic
surface passing through the sawtooth mixing radius. It identifies the outer
boundary of the plasma region homogenized during a sawtooth crash.

The coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(r_{\mathrm{mix}}) = \left(\frac{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(r_{\mathrm{mix}}) - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}{\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}} - \Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}}\right)^{1/2}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}(r_{\mathrm{mix}})$ is the normalized
toroidal flux coordinate at the mixing radius, $r_{\mathrm{mix}}$ is the
sawtooth mixing radius, $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor}}(r_{\mathrm{mix}})$ is the
toroidal magnetic flux enclosed by the mixing surface,
$\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,axis}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux at the magnetic
axis, and $\Phi_{\mathrm{tor,boundary}}$ is the toroidal magnetic flux at
the equilibrium boundary.

The scope is the single magnetic surface at the sawtooth mixing radius
within the plasma region affected by the crash. This is a locus-specific
evaluation of the broader [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate), not a coordinate
assigned to every magnetic surface, a volume average, or a flux-surface
average. It is distinct from the corresponding coordinate at the [sawtooth
inversion
radius](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_sawtooth_inversion_radius),
because the mixing radius and inversion radius represent different sawtooth
characteristics.

items.name: radial_ion_charge_state_diffusivity
items.description:
Radial ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle
diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state along the radial
direction.
items.documentation:
Radial ion charge-state diffusivity is the effective Fickian particle
diffusivity for ions in a specified ionization state along the radial
direction. It is the scalar transport coefficient that relates the radial
diffusive particle flux density of that charge state to the negative radial
gradient of its number density.

For the radial projection in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height, the defining Fickian relation is:

$$
\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,R} = -D_{s,R}\,\nabla_R n_s
$$

where $\Gamma^{\mathrm{diff}}_{s,R}$ is the radial diffusive particle flux
density of charge state $s$, $D_{s,R}$ is this diffusivity, $n_s$ is the
number density of charge state $s$, and $\nabla_R n_s =
\hat{\mathbf{R}}\cdot\nabla n_s$ is its derivative along increasing $R$.

This quantity is charge-state-resolved and applies to one ionization state,
unlike the charge-state-averaged ion diffusivity. It is the radial
counterpart of [ion charge-state
diffusivity](name:ion_charge_state_diffusivity) and is equivalent to [radial
ion charge-state diffusion
coefficient](name:radial_ion_charge_state_diffusion_coefficient) when the
same Fickian closure is used. Radial denotes the cylindrical
$\hat{\mathbf{R}}$ projection and is not synonymous with a
flux-surface-normal projection; convective transport and particle sources or
sinks are excluded.

items.name: counter_passing_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Counter-passing fast-electron collisional power density is the local rate of
kinetic-energy change of the counter-passing guiding-center component of the
suprathermal electron distribution caused by Coulomb collisions with other
plasma species. It is the counter-passing orbit-class contribution to the
fast-electron collisional energy balance, positive for energy gain by that
component and negative for energy loss.
items.documentation:
Counter-passing fast-electron collisional power density is the local rate of
change of kinetic energy density of the counter-passing component of the
fast-electron distribution caused by Coulomb collisions with other plasma
species. It is the counter-passing orbit-class contribution to the
fast-electron collisional energy balance. The counter-passing component
consists of passing guiding-center states whose bounce-averaged toroidal
angular motion is opposite to the plasma-current circulation; the toroidal
angle is $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where
$R$ is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The quantity is the kinetic-energy moment of the Coulomb collision operator
over the counter-passing part of fast-electron phase space:

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{fast,counter}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x}) = \sum_s \int \chi_{\mathrm{counter}}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, \frac{1}{2} m_e v^2\, C_{es}[f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}, f_s](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\, d^3v
$$

where the sum is over collision partners $s$, $\chi_{\mathrm{counter}}$ is
the phase-space indicator equal to one on counter-passing fast-electron
guiding-center states and zero elsewhere, $m_e$ is the electron mass,
$v=|\mathbf{v}|$ is speed, $f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ is normalized so that $\int
f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}\,d^3v$ gives the local fast-electron density, $f_s$ is
the distribution of species $s$, and $C_{es}$ is the Coulomb collision
operator giving the collisional time derivative of $f_{e,\mathrm{fast}}$ due
to species $s$. The counter-passing restriction is applied by
$\chi_{\mathrm{counter}}$; it does not redefine the collision partners. For
relativistic fast electrons, the kinetic-energy weight is replaced by the
appropriate relativistic kinetic energy.

The orbit-class partition is non-overlapping: co-passing, counter-passing,
and [trapped](name:trapped_fast_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions)
components sum to fast-electron collisional power density when the same
collision operator and phase-space partition are used. This quantity
excludes collisional energy exchange assigned to the thermal-electron
population.

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy to
the counter-passing fast-electron component.

items.name: plasma_temperature_real_part
items.description:
Real quadrature of a first-order plasma-temperature perturbation
eigenfunction, giving the component in phase with the chosen complex
reference. It denotes the real part only, not the full complex
eigenfunction.
items.documentation:
Real quadrature of a first-order plasma-temperature perturbation
eigenfunction is the in-phase scalar temperature perturbation component
associated with a linear magnetohydrodynamic mode. It denotes only the real
part of the plasma-temperature eigenfunction relative to the chosen complex
phase reference.

The complex temperature perturbation eigenfunction is decomposed into real
and imaginary quadratures as

$$
\widetilde{T} = T_R + i T_I
$$

where $\widetilde{T}$ is the complex first-order plasma-temperature
perturbation eigenfunction, $T_R$ is this real quadrature, $T_I$ is the
corresponding imaginary quadrature, and $i$ is the imaginary unit.

This parent quantity abstracts over concrete real-part plasma-temperature
perturbation names, such as [perturbed plasma temperature real
part](name:perturbed_plasma_temperature_real_part). It excludes the
imaginary quadrature, the modulus or phase of $\widetilde{T}$, and the
equilibrium plasma temperature about which the perturbation is linearized.
Changing the complex phase reference changes the numerical split between
$T_R$ and $T_I$.

Sign convention: Positive when $T_R$ represents an increase of the plasma
temperature relative to the equilibrium temperature at the chosen complex
phase reference.

items.name: toroidal_conductivity
items.description:
Electrical conductivity governing the toroidal conductive current response
to an electric field directed around the plasma symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Toroidal conductivity is the toroidal–toroidal projection of the local
electrical-conductivity tensor in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame. Here $R$ is major radius measured from the symmetry axis, $\phi$
is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; the toroidal direction
follows increasing $\phi$.

The directional coefficient is defined by

$$
\sigma_{\phi\phi} = \hat{\phi} \cdot \boldsymbol{\sigma} \cdot \hat{\phi}
$$

where $\sigma_{\phi\phi}$ is toroidal conductivity, $\boldsymbol{\sigma}$ is
the local electrical-conductivity tensor, and $\hat{\phi}$ is the toroidal
unit vector. For an electric field directed entirely toroidally, the
toroidal conductive current density satisfies $j_\phi^{\mathrm{cond}} =
\sigma_{\phi\phi} E_\phi$, where $j_\phi^{\mathrm{cond}}$ is the toroidal
current-density contribution driven by that field and $E_\phi$ is the
toroidal electric-field component.

This is a local response coefficient, with no toroidal or flux-surface
averaging implied. It is neither an angular coordinate nor a total
conductance. Cross-directional electrical responses and independently driven
current contributions are not included in this diagonal coefficient.

The [poloidal conductivity](name:poloidal_conductivity) describes the
corresponding response along the poloidal tangent. Unlike [parallel
conductivity](name:parallel_conductivity), which follows the local magnetic
field, toroidal conductivity follows a geometric direction and need not
equal the field-parallel coefficient.

items.name: z_direction_unit_vector_of_camera
items.description:
Signed Z-direction cosine of a camera’s viewing-direction unit vector in the
right-handed Cartesian (x, y, z) frame.
items.documentation:
The camera direction component along the Cartesian Z axis is the signed
directional cosine of the camera’s viewing-direction unit vector. It
specifies how strongly the viewing direction points along the positive or
negative Z direction.

The component is defined by

$$
d_z = \mathbf{d} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{z}}
$$

where $d_z$ is the Z component, $\mathbf{d}$ is the camera’s direction unit
vector, and $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the positive-Z basis vector of the
right-handed Cartesian $(x, y, z)$ frame.

This quantity applies to the viewing direction of an individual camera, with
no spatial, population, or charge-state aggregation. It is a directional
component rather than the camera position, the image-up orientation, or the
magnitude of the direction vector.

Together with the corresponding [x direction unit vector of the
camera](name:x_direction_unit_vector_of_camera) and [y direction unit vector
of the camera](name:y_direction_unit_vector_of_camera), it specifies the
complete viewing-direction vector; the three components satisfy $d_x^2 +
d_y^2 + d_z^2 = 1$, where $d_x$ and $d_y$ are the X and Y components of that
same unit vector.

items.name: second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_filter
items.description:
Second local tangential coordinate of a filter boundary point is the signed
position of that point along the filter's second in-plane basis direction in
the object-local planar frame attached to the filter.
items.documentation:
Second local tangential coordinate of a filter boundary point is the signed
scalar coordinate obtained by projecting the point's displacement from the
filter local-frame origin onto the filter's second local tangential
direction. It is paired with the [first local tangential coordinate of a
filter](name:first_local_tangential_coordinate_of_filter) to locate points
in the filter plane.

The coordinate is defined by the projection

$$
u_{2,f} = (\mathbf{r} - \mathbf{r}_{0,f}) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{t}}_{2,f}
$$

where $u_{2,f}$ is this coordinate, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector of
the filter boundary point, $\mathbf{r}_{0,f}$ is the filter local-frame
origin, and $\hat{\mathbf{t}}_{2,f}$ is the second local tangential unit
vector of the filter.

The filter local frame is object-local: $\hat{\mathbf{t}}_{1,f}$ and
$\hat{\mathbf{t}}_{2,f}$ lie in the filter plane. The first local tangential
unit vector is chosen with positive projection along increasing toroidal
angle $\phi$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame; the
second local tangential unit vector completes the oriented in-plane basis
with the filter normal, so that $\hat{\mathbf{t}}_{1,f} \times
\hat{\mathbf{t}}_{2,f}$ points along the positive filter normal. This
quantity refers to the filter boundary itself, not to the [second local
tangential coordinate of a filter
window](name:second_local_tangential_coordinate_of_filter_window).

Sign convention: Positive when the displacement from the filter local-frame
origin to the point has positive projection on the second local tangential
unit vector of the filter.

items.name: nitrogen_density
items.description:
Number density of nitrogen nuclei is the local count of nitrogen atomic
nuclei per plasma volume, summed over all charge states from neutral through
fully stripped nitrogen.
items.documentation:
Number density of nitrogen nuclei is the local count of nitrogen atomic
nuclei per plasma volume. It is a species-level elemental density, so
neutral nitrogen and every ionized nitrogen charge state are included.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
n_N = \sum_{z=0}^{7} n_{N,z}
$$

where $n_N$ is the nitrogen density, $n_{N,z}$ is the number density of
nitrogen nuclei in charge state $z$, $z=0$ denotes neutral nitrogen, and
$z=7$ denotes fully stripped nitrogen because nitrogen has atomic number
$7$.

This quantity is local and is distinct from [line-averaged nitrogen
density](name:line_averaged_nitrogen_density) and [volume-averaged nitrogen
density](name:volume_averaged_nitrogen_density), which are spatial averages
of the same charge-state-summed species density. In the absence of a
population qualifier, the density includes thermal, fast, and other
nonthermal nitrogen nuclei.

items.name: mhd_mode_reference_phase
items.description:
Signed angular offset that fixes the complex phase of a mode relative to its
zero-phase reference.
items.documentation:
A mode reference phase is the angular offset applied to a complex
perturbation or eigenfunction to establish its phase relative to a
zero-phase reference. It specifies phase orientation without defining the
mode number, amplitude, or geometric position angle.

For a complex mode amplitude, the reference phase is represented by

$$
\tilde{X} = |\tilde{X}| e^{i\phi_{\rm ref}}
$$

where $\tilde{X}$ is the complex perturbation amplitude, $|\tilde{X}|$ is
its magnitude, and $\phi_{\rm ref}$ is the reference phase. The quantity
generalizes the phase used by
[linear_mhd_mode_reference_phase](name:linear_mhd_mode_reference_phase) and
is the phase component of [mode_reference_phase](name:mode_reference_phase).

Sign convention: Positive when the complex mode phase is advanced in the
defined angular direction from its zero-phase reference.

items.name: thermal_electron_power_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Volume-integrated Coulomb-collisional power transferred from fast
non-Maxwellian particles to bulk thermal electrons across trapped and
passing orbit classes, with positive values indicating electron heating.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net Coulomb-collisional energy-transfer rate into the
bulk thermal-electron population from fast non-Maxwellian particles. It is
the thermal-electron component of electron power due to collisions,
including the represented trapped and passing orbit classes.

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}} = \int_V p_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $P_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}$ is the volume-integrated power,
$p_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local
[thermal-electron collisional power
density](name:thermal_electron_power_density_due_to_collisions), $V$ is the
integration volume, and $\mathbf{x}$ is position. The quantity includes
energy received by thermal electrons and excludes the corresponding
donor-side energy change represented by [fast-particle collisional
power](name:fast_particle_power_due_to_collisions). Positive values denote
net heating of the bulk thermal-electron population.

items.name: lower_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface
items.description:
Dimensionless Luce shape coefficient for the lower outboard quadrant of
nested magnetic flux surfaces, measuring signed departure from a reference
ellipse with the same center, horizontal half-width, and elongation.
items.documentation:
The lower outer squareness $\zeta_{\rm lo}$ is the dimensionless Luce (2013)
shape coefficient for the lower outboard ($-Z$, larger-$R$) corner of each
nested magnetic flux surface, measuring its departure from a reference
ellipse sharing the same center, horizontal half-width, and elongation.

At the modeled lower outboard corner, the reference condition is

$$
\zeta_{\rm lo}=0 \Longleftrightarrow \mathcal{C}_{\rm lo}=\mathcal{E}_{\rm lo}
$$

where $\zeta_{\rm lo}$ is the lower outer squareness coefficient,
$\mathcal{C}_{\rm lo}$ is the modeled lower outboard corner, and
$\mathcal{E}_{\rm lo}$ is the corresponding reference ellipse. The
cross-section is described in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height.

This coefficient selects the lower outboard quadrant and is the lower
component of [outer squareness](name:outer_squareness_of_flux_surface),
complementing [upper outer
squareness](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_flux_surface). Up-down asymmetry
allows the two quadrant-specific coefficients to differ; positive values
describe boxier outward corners, while negative values describe corners
indented relative to the reference ellipse.

Sign convention: Positive when the modeled lower outboard corner extends
toward increasing $R$ beyond the corresponding reference ellipse in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: co_passing_thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Local Coulomb-collisional energy transfer from co-passing nonthermal
particles to thermal ions of a specified species, summed over all ionic
charge states.
items.documentation:
Co-passing thermal-ion collisional power density is the local signed rate of
kinetic-energy transfer from the co-passing part of a fast or non-Maxwellian
particle distribution to thermal ions of a specified species. The co-passing
restriction selects untrapped donor trajectories, not recipient-ion orbits.

By conservation of energy in pairwise Coulomb collisions, the recipient
power density is the negative of the corresponding donor kinetic-energy
moment:

$$
P_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{co}}(\mathbf{x}) = -\sum_a\sum_q \int \frac{1}{2}m_a|\mathbf{v}|^2 C_{a,iq}\!\left[f_a^{\mathrm{co}},f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}\right](\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $P_{i,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the thermal-ion power density at
spatial position $\mathbf{x}$, $i$ identifies the recipient ion species, $q$
is its ionic charge number, and $a$ indexes species represented in the
donating distribution. The quantity $m_a$ is the donor particle mass,
$\mathbf{v}$ is donor velocity, $f_a^{\mathrm{co}}$ is the co-passing donor
distribution, and $f_{iq}^{\mathrm{th}}$ is the thermal recipient
distribution for charge state $q$. The Coulomb collision operator $C_{a,iq}$
gives the collisional time derivative of the donor distribution due to that
recipient population; the integral covers all donor velocities.

The recipient contribution is summed over all ionic charge states of the
specified species, not over different recipient species. The thermal
qualifier identifies the recipient population, not the donors; energy
deposited in electrons or fast-ion recipients is excluded. This quantity
retains local spatial variation across a poloidal cross-section and includes
neither flux-surface averaging nor volume integration.

It is the co-passing donor contribution to [thermal-ion collisional power
density](name:thermal_ion_power_density_due_to_collisions); adding the
counter-passing and trapped donor contributions recovers that parent
quantity. Its flux-surface average equals the charge-state sum of the
[flux-surface-averaged co-passing thermal-ion charge-state
contributions](name:co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_power_density_due_to_collisions).

Sign convention: Positive when Coulomb collisions transfer kinetic energy
from the co-passing donor population to the specified thermal-ion
population.

items.name: bulk_center_of_mass_velocity
items.description:
Center-of-mass velocity is the mass-weighted barycentric velocity vector of
a multicomponent plasma, equal to total momentum density divided by total
mass density.
items.documentation:
Center-of-mass velocity is the mass-weighted barycentric velocity vector of
a multicomponent plasma. It is the velocity whose product with total mass
density equals the total plasma momentum density of the species included in
the plasma mixture.

The center-of-mass velocity $\mathbf{V}_{cm}$ is defined as total momentum
density divided by total mass density:

$$
\mathbf{V}_{cm} = \frac{\sum_s m_s n_s \mathbf{v}_s}{\sum_s m_s n_s} = \frac{\sum_s \rho_s \mathbf{v}_s}{\rho}
$$

where $s$ indexes the included plasma species, $m_s$ is the particle mass of
species $s$, $n_s$ is its number density, $\mathbf{v}_s$ is its fluid
velocity, $\rho_s = m_s n_s$ is its mass-density contribution, and $\rho =
\sum_s \rho_s$ is the total mass density.

The quantity represents the full velocity vector of the included
multicomponent plasma mixture and is aggregated over those species by mass
density. It is not a single-species velocity, an unweighted species average,
a number-density-weighted average, or one selected directional projection.

The [center-of-mass velocity](name:center_of_mass_velocity) provides the
common barycentric reference from which directional components are formed.
For example, [poloidal bulk center-of-mass
velocity](name:poloidal_bulk_center_of_mass_velocity) is the projection of
this vector onto the positive poloidal tangent of its specified
flux-coordinate system.

Sign convention: Positive when a resolved component of $\mathbf{V}_{cm}$
points along the positive direction of its declared basis; cylindrical
components follow increasing $R$, $\phi$, or $Z$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, while a poloidal component follows the
positive tangent of the specified flux coordinate $(\rho,\theta,\phi)$.

items.name: bandwidth_of_ece_channel
items.description:
Full-width frequency interval passed by the intermediate-frequency bandpass
filter of an electron-cyclotron-emission radiometer channel, setting the
emission frequencies contributing to its radiation-temperature signal.
items.documentation:
The bandwidth is the total frequency span passed by the
intermediate-frequency bandpass filter associated with one
electron-cyclotron-emission radiometer channel. It characterizes the
channel's accepted spectral interval rather than an emission intensity or a
plasma frequency.

The full width is defined by

$$
\Delta f_{\mathrm{IF}} = f_{\mathrm{high}} - f_{\mathrm{low}}
$$

where $\Delta f_{\mathrm{IF}}$ is the intermediate-frequency bandwidth,
$f_{\mathrm{high}}$ is the upper bandpass edge frequency, and
$f_{\mathrm{low}}$ is the lower bandpass edge frequency.

This quantity applies to one ECE channel and uses the full-width convention;
it is not the center frequency, a reference carrier frequency, or a
wavelength-domain response width such as the [effective spectral width of a
spectrometer
channel](name:effective_spectral_width_of_spectrometer_channel). The
accepted interval determines which electron-cyclotron-emission frequencies
contribute to the [radiative temperature at an ECE
channel](name:radiative_temperature_at_ece_channel) and can therefore affect
the channel's effective radial localization.

items.name: resistivity_of_limiter_tile
items.description:
Electrical resistivity of material forming an individual limiter unit,
governing the local relation between electric field and current density
during electromagnetic response.
items.documentation:
Electrical resistivity of a limiter unit is the material property that
determines how strongly its conducting material opposes electric current and
converts electromagnetic energy into ohmic dissipation.

The local constitutive relation is

$$
\mathbf{E} = \rho\mathbf{J}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the electric-field vector, $\rho$ is the electrical
resistivity, and $\mathbf{J}$ is the conventional electric-current-density
vector.

This quantity applies to the material of one limiter unit and represents a
local material property rather than a sum over limiter units or a lumped
electrical resistance of an entire structure. It excludes geometric path
effects, contact contributions, and circuit-level inductive effects. The
limiter-unit property is the component-specific counterpart of
[resistivity_of_plasma_facing_component](name:resistivity_of_plasma_facing_component)
and is distinct from the effective material property assigned to a broader
wall through
[resistivity_of_wall_material](name:resistivity_of_wall_material).

items.name: torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Local rate at which collisions transfer angular momentum to or from a plasma
population, expressed as torque per unit volume.
items.documentation:
Collisional torque density is the local angular-momentum transfer rate
imparted to a specified plasma population by collisional interactions,
divided by volume. It applies to electron, ion, charge-state, and
orbit-class populations, including the specific cases represented by
[electron collisional torque
density](name:electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions) and [ion
collisional torque density](name:ion_torque_density_due_to_collisions).

For a resolved scalar torque component, the defining relation is

$$
\tau_{s,\mathrm{coll}} = \left.\frac{\partial \ell_s}{\partial t}\right|_{\mathrm{coll}}
$$

where $\tau_{s,\mathrm{coll}}$ is the collisional torque density, $\ell_s$
is the corresponding angular-momentum density of population $s$, and the
subscript indicates that only collisional transfer is included.

The quantity excludes torque caused by electromagnetic forces, pressure
forces, or other noncollisional processes. More specific population and
orbit restrictions, such as co-passing fast-ion charge-state collisional
torque density, refine the recipient population without changing the
underlying definition.

Sign convention: Positive when collisions increase the resolved angular
momentum of the recipient population.

items.name: ion_torque
items.description:
Volume-integrated torque vector acting on the ion population, representing
the net source or sink of ion angular momentum while retaining its
direction.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the net torque vector exerted on the ion population and
integrated over the relevant plasma volume. It represents the global source
or sink of ion angular momentum, with ionic charge states aggregated rather
than represented separately.

$$
\boldsymbol{T}_i = \int_V \boldsymbol{\tau}_i(\mathbf{x})\,dV
$$

where $\boldsymbol{T}_i$ is the integrated ion torque vector,
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_i$ is the local [ion torque
density](name:ion_torque_density), $V$ is the integration volume, and
$\mathbf{x}$ is position. The quantity includes the contributing ion species
and charge states; the [toroidal ion
torque](name:toroidal_explicit_ion_torque) is its toroidal component about
the toroidal symmetry axis.

Sign convention: Positive when a vector component points along the
corresponding positive direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi,
Z)$ frame.

items.name: radial_outline_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of each contour point defining a fiber-optic current
sensor boundary in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial outline coordinate gives the major radius of each point on the
geometric boundary of a fiber-optic current sensor in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, phi, Z)$ frame.

The major radius is the perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry
axis. In a right-handed Cartesian basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$ with
$\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$, it is defined by:

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2+y^2}
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, and $x$ and $y$ are Cartesian
coordinates perpendicular to the vertical axis.

The quantity is evaluated independently at each outline point and is
distinct from the signed vertical coordinate, represented by the
corresponding [vertical outline
coordinate](name:vertical_outline_of_fiber_optic_current_sensor). As a
radial distance, it is non-negative.

items.name: total_incident_power_of_divertor
items.description:
Total incident power of the divertor is the rate of plasma energy arrival at
all target surfaces through conduction, convection, radiation, and other
incident channels.
items.documentation:
Total incident power of the divertor is the incoming plasma energy rate
summed over all divertor target surfaces. It aggregates all physical
contributions to the incident power rather than selecting a single target or
energy-transfer channel.

The defining aggregation is

$$
P = \sum_{i \in \mathcal{D}} \sum_{c \in \mathcal{C}} P_{i,c}
$$

where $P$ is the total incident power, $\mathcal{D}$ is the complete set of
divertor target surfaces, $i$ identifies a target, $\mathcal{C}$ is the
complete set of nonoverlapping incident-power categories, $c$ identifies a
category, and $P_{i,c}$ is the power incident on target $i$ through category
$c$.

The channel sum includes conducted, convected, radiated, and other incident
contributions without double counting. The quantity counts incoming energy
before subtracting reflected energy or outgoing thermal radiation; it is not
the net power retained by the target material. Thermal radiation emitted by
the targets is not an incoming contribution.

The [absorbed radiated power of the
divertor](name:absorbed_radiated_power_of_divertor) accounts only for
radiation retained after reflection, rather than the full incident load. The
[power at a divertor target](name:power_at_divertor_target) describes
deposition on one target, whereas this quantity aggregates incident power
over all targets.

items.name: shattered_pellet_species_number_density_of_pellet_fragment
items.description:
Number density of a specified atomic species within the solid material of an
individual shattered-pellet fragment.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the local volumetric abundance of one selected atomic
species in the material composing an individual shattered-pellet fragment.

It is defined by

$$
n_s = \frac{N_s}{V_f}
$$

where $n_s$ is the number density of the selected atomic species, $N_s$ is
its number of constituent atoms in the fragment, and $V_f$ is the physical
volume occupied by the fragment.

The scope is restricted to one fragment and one specified atomic species in
the fragment material. The quantity is species-selective rather than summed
over different species, and it describes pellet composition rather than the
number density of particles in the surrounding plasma. No plasma
ionization-state aggregation or charge-state resolution is implied.

Multiplying this density by the fragment volume gives the corresponding
constituent-atom count. It therefore provides a fragment-local density
counterpart to the whole-pellet inventory represented by atomic count of
pellet, while [fast neutral internal state number
density](name:fast_neutral_internal_state_number_density) describes a
plasma-particle population distinguished by internal state.

items.name: vertical_magnetization_of_ferritic_element
items.description:
Signed vertical component of the effective magnetization vector assigned to
a ferritic element in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
Vertical magnetization of a ferritic element is the signed projection of its
assigned effective magnetization vector onto the vertical direction in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

The defining projection is:

$$
M_Z^{\mathrm{eff}} = \mathbf{M}^{\mathrm{eff}} \cdot \hat{\mathbf{Z}}
$$

where $M_Z^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the vertical magnetization component,
$\mathbf{M}^{\mathrm{eff}}$ is the effective magnetization vector assigned
to the ferritic element, and $\hat{\mathbf{Z}}$ is the unit vector toward
increasing vertical height. The corresponding radial projection is [radial
magnetization of a ferritic
element](name:radial_magnetization_of_ferritic_element); neither quantity is
the magnetic field at the element centroid, such as the [vertical magnetic
field at a ferritic element
centroid](name:vertical_magnetic_field_at_ferritic_element_centroid).

Sign convention: Positive when the effective magnetization vector has a
component toward increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: power_at_wall_due_to_conduction
items.description:
Thermal power deposited on all plasma-facing wall and divertor surfaces by
parallel electron and ion heat conduction along open scrape-off-layer
magnetic field lines, excluding convective, radiative, and neutral-particle
channels.
items.documentation:
The power at the wall due to conduction is the thermal energy deposited on
all plasma-facing wall and divertor surfaces by electron and ion heat
conduction along open scrape-off-layer magnetic field lines. It excludes
convective particle enthalpy, absorbed radiation, and neutral-particle
energy deposition.

The defining surface integral is:

$$
P_{\mathrm{wall,cond}} = \int_{S_{\mathrm{wall}}} \left(\mathbf{q}_{e,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}} + \mathbf{q}_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}\right) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\,\mathrm{d}A
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{wall,cond}}$ is the deposited conductive power,
$S_{\mathrm{wall}}$ is the union of all plasma-facing wall and divertor
surfaces, $\mathbf{q}_{e,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ and
$\mathbf{q}_{i,\parallel}^{\mathrm{cond}}$ are the electron and ion
conductive heat-flux vectors along open magnetic field lines,
$\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the plasma toward the
material, and $\mathrm{d}A$ is a surface-area element.

This quantity is the all-wall member of [power due to
conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction). Restricting the selected surfaces
to all divertor targets gives [power of divertor due to
conduction](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_conduction), while a single target
contribution is represented by [power at divertor target due to
conduction](name:power_at_divertor_target_due_to_conduction).

items.name: volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Number density of free electrons averaged over the plasma volume inside the
last closed flux surface, including thermal and nonthermal populations.
items.documentation:
Number density of electron

The volume average of the local [electron density](name:electron_density) is
defined by

$$
\langle n_e\rangle_V = \frac{1}{V}\int_V n_e\,dV
$$

where $n_e$ is the local free-electron number density, $\langle
n_e\rangle_V$ is its volume average, $V$ is the plasma volume enclosed by
the last closed flux surface and specifies the integration region, and $dV$
is a physical volume element. Multiplying the average by that volume gives
the total number of free electrons inside the boundary.

All free-electron populations, including thermal and nonthermal electrons,
are included; electrons bound in atoms, molecules, or ions are excluded.
Plasma outside the last closed flux surface is excluded from the average.
Unlike [line-averaged electron
density](name:line_averaged_electron_density), this quantity is a
physical-volume mean rather than a chord mean.

The same spatial averaging applies to [volume-averaged ion
density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density), but that quantity counts the
specified ion population rather than electrons. This electron mean supplies
the denominator of abundance ratios such as the [ratio of volume-averaged
carbon density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_carbon_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density);
such a ratio uses separately averaged densities over the same volume, not a
volume average of their local ratio.

items.name: electron_power_at_inner_divertor_target
items.description:
Rate at which incident electron energy is deposited on the high-field-side
inner divertor target, integrated over its wetted strike-zone surface.
items.documentation:
Electron power at the inner divertor target is the rate at which energy
carried by incident electrons is deposited on the high-field-side divertor
target surface. It is the electron-channel contribution to the total target
load, rather than the combined contribution of all incident energy channels.

The deposited electron power is defined by the surface integral

$$
P_{e,\mathrm{inner}} = \int_{A_{\mathrm{wet,inner}}} q_{e,\mathrm{dep}}(\mathbf{x})\,dA
$$

where $A_{\mathrm{wet,inner}}$ is the wetted inner-target area,
$q_{e,\mathrm{dep}}$ is the electron energy-deposition flux density in W
m$^{-2}$, and $dA$ is an element of target surface area in m$^2$. The result
is the electron contribution to power at the inner divertor target; ion
energy is represented separately by ion power at the inner divertor target,
while neutral and radiative contributions are excluded.

items.name: toroidal_coordinate_at_shattering_position
items.description:
Toroidal azimuthal coordinate of the point where the pellet center-of-mass
trajectory intersects the shattering element.
items.documentation:
The toroidal coordinate of the shattering position is the azimuthal
coordinate of the intersection between the pellet center-of-mass trajectory
and the shattering element.

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, its coordinate is
defined by

$$
\mathbf{r}_s = R_s(\cos\phi_s\,\hat{x} + \sin\phi_s\,\hat{y}) + Z_s\hat{z}
$$

where $\mathbf{r}_s$ is the shattering-position vector, $R_s$ is its
major-radius coordinate, $Z_s$ is its vertical coordinate, $\phi_s$ is this
toroidal coordinate, and $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ is the right-handed
Cartesian basis with $\hat{z}=\hat{Z}$.

This event-location coordinate is distinct from the [toroidal coordinate at
a pellet path point](name:toroidal_coordinate_at_pellet_path_point) and from
the [toroidal coordinate of a pellet
fragment](name:toroidal_coordinate_of_pellet_fragment), which refer to
different physical locations.

Sign convention: Positive when the angular displacement from the $\phi=0$
reference is in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: co_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Co-passing collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum
transfer per plasma volume to a specified thermal ion charge state from
Coulomb collisions with co-passing particles.
items.documentation:
Co-passing collisional torque density is the vector rate of angular-momentum
transfer per unit plasma volume to thermal ions of a specified charge state
from Coulomb collisions with the co-passing population.

With $\mathrm{co}$ denoting this collision channel, the local torque density
is defined by the moment of the collisional force density:

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}} = \mathbf{r} \times \mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{co}}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the torque-density vector,
$\mathbf{r}$ is the position vector from the toroidal symmetry axis to the
local plasma volume, and $\mathbf{R}_{\mathrm{co}}$ is the collisional force
density exerted on the specified thermal ion charge state by co-passing
particles. The charge-state selection is retained rather than summed over
ionization states. This is the co-passing contribution to [thermal ion
charge-state collisional torque
density](name:thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
and differs from the corresponding [counter-passing
quantity](name:counter_passing_thermal_ion_charge_state_torque_density_due_to_collisions)
by the collision-partner orbit class.

Sign convention: Positive when a component of
$\boldsymbol{\tau}_{\mathrm{co}}$ points along the corresponding positive
direction of the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ basis, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ increases toroidally, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Effective coefficient relating an ion population's density-normalized
diffusive energy flux to its temperature gradient, without selecting a
transport direction.
items.documentation:
The ion energy diffusion coefficient characterizes gradient-driven energy
transport for the ion population represented by an energy-transport closure.
It is the ion specialization of the [energy diffusion
coefficient](name:energy_diffusion_coefficient), distinct from coefficients
describing particle transport and from separately represented convective or
advective energy fluxes.

The defining scalar Fickian closure is:

$$
\frac{\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}}{n_i} = -D_{i,W}\,\nabla T_i
$$

where $\mathbf{Q}_{i,\mathrm{diff}}$ is the diffusive thermal-energy flux
carried by the included ions, $n_i$ is their number density, $T_i$ is their
temperature expressed as thermal energy per particle, and $D_{i,W}$ is the
effective diffusion coefficient. The subscripts $i$ and $W$ identify ions
and the energy channel, respectively, and $\nabla$ denotes the spatial
gradient. The minus sign specifies down-gradient transport for a positive
coefficient.

At species level, the population includes all charge states: number density
is summed, while temperature is the density-weighted mean over all charge
states. The coefficient is an intensive effective closure coefficient, not a
sum of charge-state coefficients. When charge states share the same
temperature gradient, their aggregate coefficient is their density-weighted
mean over all charge states. The [ion charge-state energy diffusion
coefficient](name:ion_charge_state_energy_diffusion_coefficient) instead
applies to one specified charge state.

No restriction to a thermal-ion subpopulation or particular transport
direction is imposed. The [thermal-ion
specialization](name:thermal_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) restricts the
population, while the [total-ion
specialization](name:total_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) describes the
aggregate ion energy channel. Directional variants such as the [parallel ion
energy diffusion
coefficient](name:parallel_ion_energy_diffusion_coefficient) select a
transport direction; the direction-unspecified parent does not imply
isotropic transport.

items.name: squareness_of_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Squareness of the plasma boundary is a dimensionless Luce shape coefficient
quantifying the whole-boundary corner deviation of the last closed flux
surface from the reference ellipse set by the boundary minor radius,
elongation, and triangularity. Positive values make the corner regions
boxier, approaching the circumscribing rectangle; negative values make them
more diamond-like.
items.documentation:
Squareness of the plasma boundary is a dimensionless Luce shape coefficient
quantifying the deviation of the corner regions of the last closed flux
surface from the reference ellipse whose semi-axes are set by the boundary
minor radius, elongation, and triangularity. It is the whole-boundary
summary of the quadrant-level squareness values, characterizing whether the
poloidal cross-section corners bulge outward toward the circumscribing
rectangle or are pinched inward relative to the elliptical reference
contour.

In a poloidal cross-section at fixed toroidal angle $\phi$ of the
right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, each quadrant of the boundary
is bounded by its radial extremum (innermost or outermost major-radius
point) and its vertical extremum (topmost or bottommost point), and a
reference ellipse is constructed through these two extrema; the semi-axes of
this ellipse are fixed by the boundary minor radius, elongation, and
triangularity. Along the diagonal from the ellipse center $O$ toward the
corner $F$ of the rectangle circumscribing the quadrant, the quadrant
squareness is

$$
\zeta = \frac{\overline{OD} - \overline{OE}}{\overline{OF} - \overline{OE}}
$$

where $D$ is the intersection of the diagonal with the plasma boundary, $E$
its intersection with the reference ellipse, and $\overline{OD}$,
$\overline{OE}$, $\overline{OF}$ are distances from the ellipse center. With
this construction $\zeta = 0$ when the boundary follows the elliptical arc,
$\zeta = 1$ when it passes through the rectangle corner, and $\zeta < 0$
when the corner is indented inside the ellipse (diamond- or bean-like).

This whole-boundary quantity summarizes the four quadrant-resolved members
[upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary),
[upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:upper_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary),
[lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary),
and
[lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:lower_outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary),
and decomposes into
[inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:inner_squareness_of_plasma_boundary)
on the high-field side (smaller major radius $R$) and
[outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary](name:outer_squareness_of_plasma_boundary)
on the low-field side (larger $R$). Use the quadrant- or side-resolved
members when the boundary corners are shaped asymmetrically; this quantity
carries no information about up-down or in-out asymmetry of the corner
shaping.

items.name: inverse_of_major_radius
items.description:
Reciprocal major-radius coordinate for a geometric point or specified
location, serving as a positive geometric factor in toroidal equilibrium
relations.
items.documentation:
Reciprocal major radius is the inverse of the perpendicular distance from
the toroidal symmetry axis to a geometric point or specified location. It is
a geometric quantity used to represent the radial dependence of toroidal
equilibrium relations.

$$
R^{-1} = \frac{1}{R}
$$

where $R$ is the [major radius](name:major_radius), namely the radial
coordinate in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

At the parent level, the quantity is evaluated pointwise or at a specified
geometric location and has no averaging or integration implied. It is
positive wherever the major radius is positive, and it is distinct from the
major radius itself because it reverses the radial dependence rather than
specifying the distance from the symmetry axis.

A flux-surface-averaged instance applies the flux-surface averaging
operation to this reciprocal quantity;
[flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_major_radius](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_major_radius)
is the corresponding geometric coefficient obtained by averaging over a
magnetic flux surface.

items.name: normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_constraint_position
items.description:
Normalized toroidal flux coordinate at the constraint position gives a
magnetic-surface label ranging from zero at the magnetic axis to one at the
equilibrium boundary.
items.documentation:
Normalized toroidal flux coordinate

At the constraint position, the coordinate is defined by

$$
\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}} = \rho_{\mathrm{tor}}/\rho_{\mathrm{tor,b}}
$$

where $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,norm}}$ is the normalized toroidal flux coordinate
at the constraint position, $\rho_{\mathrm{tor}}$ is the unnormalized
toroidal flux coordinate of the magnetic surface containing that position,
and $\rho_{\mathrm{tor,b}}$ is its [value at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_plasma_boundary).

The quantity applies pointwise at one specified constraint position,
independently of which physical quantity is constrained; it is not an
average over positions or a sum over constraints. It specifies a
magnetic-surface label, not the constrained physical quantity, an
unnormalized flux radius, or a geometric distance.

It is the locus-specific evaluation of the parent [normalized toroidal flux
coordinate](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate). For nested closed
magnetic surfaces and a nonzero boundary coordinate, it spans zero at the
magnetic axis to one at the equilibrium boundary. When that boundary is a
separatrix, the outer endpoint is the [normalized toroidal flux coordinate
at the separatrix](name:normalized_toroidal_flux_coordinate_at_separatrix).

items.name: toroidal_ion_velocity
items.description:
Signed projection of an ion species' bulk flow along the geometric toroidal
direction, using the density-weighted mean over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
The toroidal ion velocity is the projection of the bulk [ion
velocity](name:ion_velocity) onto the direction of increasing toroidal angle
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It describes mean
directed motion rather than random thermal motion.

The projection, including charge-state averaging, is defined by

$$
v_{i\phi}=\mathbf{v}_i\cdot\hat{\phi}=\frac{\sum_q n_{iq}\,\mathbf{v}_{iq}\cdot\hat{\phi}}{\sum_q n_{iq}}
$$

where $v_{i\phi}$ is the toroidal ion velocity, $\mathbf{v}_i$ is the
charge-state-averaged ion bulk velocity, $i$ identifies the selected ion
species, $q$ labels its ionic charge states, $n_{iq}$ is the number density
of each charge state, and $\mathbf{v}_{iq}$ is its mean velocity vector. The
unit vector $\hat{\phi}$ points toward increasing toroidal angle $\phi$; $R$
is major radius and $Z$ is vertical height.

The sums include all ionic charge states of the selected species and exclude
neutrals. The result is a density-weighted mean, not a sum of charge-state
velocities or a combination of distinct ion species. Unlike [plasma
velocity](name:plasma_velocity), it does not represent the mass-weighted
flow of all plasma species. It is a linear velocity component, not a speed
magnitude or an angular rotation rate; no spatial averaging or fixed
evaluation locus is implied.

Dividing this component by the total magnetic-field magnitude gives the
[ratio of toroidal ion velocity to magnetic-field
magnitude](name:ratio_of_toroidal_ion_velocity_to_magnetic_field_magnitude).

Sign convention: Positive when the ion bulk flow projects toward increasing
toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when viewed from above.

items.name: neon_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the neon ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local neon-ion count per physical volume at that location,
summed over all ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the neon ion population evaluated at the magnetic
axis is the local neon-ion count per physical volume at that location,
summed over all neon ionic charge states. It represents neon ions
specifically, rather than neutral neon, electrons, or another plasma
population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{\mathrm{Ne,axis}} = \sum_{q=1}^{Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}} n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{\mathrm{Ne,axis}}$ is the total neon-ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $n_{\mathrm{Ne}^{q+},\mathrm{axis}}$ is the number density of
neon ions with charge state $q$ at that location, $q$ is the positive ionic
charge-state index, and $Z_{\mathrm{Ne}}$ is the atomic number of neon.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the neon-ion population at that location and is
summed over ionic charge states; neutral neon is excluded, and the quantity
is neither a flux-surface nor a volume integral.

This is the neon-specific realization of the population-independent [density
at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). It has the same locus
and charge-state aggregation convention as [oxygen density at the magnetic
axis](name:oxygen_density_at_magnetic_axis), but counts neon ions rather
than oxygen ions.

items.name: reference_calibration_wavelength_of_spectrometer_channel
items.description:
Reference calibration wavelength of a spectrometer channel is the zero-pixel
intercept of its linear pixel-to-vacuum-wavelength relation.
items.documentation:
Wavelength of spectrometer channel

The defining calibration relation is

$$
\lambda(k) = g\,k + \lambda_{\mathrm{off}}
$$

where $\lambda(k)$ is the calibrated vacuum [wavelength] assigned to pixel
index $k$, $g$ is the dispersion gain giving the wavelength change per index
increment, and $\lambda_{\mathrm{off}}$ is the reference calibration
wavelength. Pixel indexing starts at one.

The intercept is the extrapolated value at zero pixel index, not the
wavelength assigned to the first pixel; the latter is
$\lambda(1)=g+\lambda_{\mathrm{off}}$. Its calibration-intercept role is
distinct from the response-center role of the [reference wavelength of a
spectrometer channel](name:reference_wavelength_of_spectrometer_channel).

items.name: accumulated_helium_3_count_due_to_gas_injection
items.description:
Cumulative equivalent-electron inventory of helium-3 atoms delivered by gas
injection after plasma breakdown, assigning two count units to each atom.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the cumulative post-breakdown inventory of helium-3 atoms
delivered by gas injection, expressed as an equivalent-electron count. It
represents delivered atomic inventory, not the number of free plasma
electrons or the ionization state of the helium-3.

$$
N_{\mathrm{eq}}(t)=Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}\int_{t_{\mathrm{bd}}}^{t}\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}(t')\,dt'
$$

Here, $N_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is the dimensionless equivalent-electron count,
$Z_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}=2$ is the helium-3 atomic number,
$\dot{N}_{\mathrm{He\text{-}3}}$ is the helium-3 atom delivery rate in atoms
per second, $t$ and $t'$ are times in seconds, and $t_{\mathrm{bd}}$ is the
plasma-breakdown time.

The quantity includes only helium-3 delivered after breakdown and is
cumulative rather than instantaneous. The corresponding instantaneous
delivery rate is [helium-3 source rate due to gas
injection](name:helium_3_source_rate_due_to_gas_injection), while
[accumulated helium-3 prefill count due to gas
injection](name:accumulated_helium_3_prefill_count_due_to_gas_injection)
covers delivery before breakdown.

items.name: fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power
items.description:
Total coherent-wave power absorbed by the suprathermal ion population,
integrated over the plasma volume and excluding thermal-ion absorption.
items.documentation:
The fast ion absorbed wave power is the volume-integrated power delivered by
coherent electromagnetic waves to the suprathermal, nonthermal ion
population through wave-particle interactions.

$$
P_{\mathrm{fast\,ion}} = \int_{V_{\mathrm{plasma}}} p_{\mathrm{abs,fast\,ion}}(\mathbf{r})\,\mathrm{d}V
$$

where $P_{\mathrm{fast\,ion}}$ is the total absorbed power,
$p_{\mathrm{abs,fast\,ion}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local power-absorption
density for fast ions at position $\mathbf{r}$, and $V_{\mathrm{plasma}}$ is
the plasma volume. This quantity is the fast-ion component of [ion absorbed
wave power](name:ion_absorbed_wave_power), excluding power absorbed by
thermal ions and electrons. It is aggregated over the coherent-wave channels
and toroidal modes represented by the global quantity; [per-toroidal-mode
fast-ion absorbed wave
power](name:per_toroidal_mode_fast_ion_absorbed_wave_power) and [fast-ion
power at an inside flux surface](name:fast_ion_power_at_inside_flux_surface)
provide more resolved scopes.

items.name: electron_volumetric_source_rate
items.description:
Electron volumetric source rate is the signed local rate of free-electron
production or removal per physical volume, entering the source term in the
electron density continuity equation.
items.documentation:
Electron volumetric source rate is the signed local rate of free-electron
production or removal per physical volume. It contributes to the source term
in the electron particle-number continuity equation.

The local particle balance is

$$
\frac{\partial n_e}{\partial t}+\nabla\cdot\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e=S_{e,\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_k S_{e,k}
$$

where $n_e$ is free-electron number density, $t$ is time,
$\boldsymbol{\Gamma}_e$ is electron particle flux density, $\nabla\cdot$
denotes spatial divergence, $S_{e,\mathrm{tot}}$ is the total volumetric
electron source rate, $S_{e,k}$ is the $k$th additive electron source
contribution, and $k$ indexes those contributions. The documented quantity
may be an individual contribution or the total source; the total is the
algebraic sum of its contributions.

This quantity applies locally to the free-electron population, without a
thermal-population or orbit-class restriction, and is neither
volume-integrated nor inherently flux-surface-averaged. An individual
decomposed contribution need not include every production or loss process; a
contribution may be independent of electron density, but density
independence is not intrinsic to the quantity. Spatial transport represented
by the flux-divergence term is distinct from the source, so the source rate
alone is not generally the time derivative of electron density. It describes
particle-number change, not energy transfer as described by [electron power
density](name:electron_power_density).

Integrating the total source over the plasma volume gives the [total
electron source rate](name:total_electron_source_rate); integrating it over
the volume enclosed by a magnetic flux surface gives the [cumulative inside
flux-surface electron particle source
rate](name:cumulative_inside_flux_surface_electron_particle_source_rate).
Integrating an individual contribution gives its contribution to those
volume-integrated rates. The corresponding ion quantity is the [ion-state
source rate](name:ion_state_source_rate), which applies to an ion charge
state rather than free electrons.

Sign convention: Positive when the source adds free electrons to the
electron population.

items.name: vacuum_poloidal_current_function
items.description:
Vacuum poloidal current function is the signed product of major radius and
the combined external-coil toroidal magnetic field, excluding plasma-induced
modifications.
items.documentation:
Vacuum poloidal current function is the major-radius-weighted toroidal
magnetic field produced by the combined external coils, excluding
plasma-induced modifications. It is the vacuum specialization of the
[poloidal current function](name:poloidal_current_function).

In the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, it is defined by

$$
F = R B_{\phi}
$$

where $F$ is the vacuum poloidal current function, $R$ is major radius
measured from the symmetry axis, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical
height, and $B_{\phi}$ is the vacuum toroidal magnetic-field component in
the direction of increasing $\phi$.

In an axisymmetric, current-free vacuum region, $F$ is spatially constant
and the toroidal field varies inversely with major radius. Equivalently, $F
= R_0 B_0$, where $R_0$ is a reference major radius and $B_0$ is the vacuum
toroidal magnetic field evaluated there.

This quantity is the field product itself, not its [change relative to an
initial
value](name:difference_of_vacuum_poloidal_current_function_and_initial_vacuum_poloidal_current_function).
That change is $F-F_{\mathrm{initial}}$, where $F_{\mathrm{initial}}$ is the
initial vacuum poloidal current function.

Sign convention: Positive when the vacuum toroidal magnetic field points in
the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$, counterclockwise when
viewed from above.

items.name: total_power_at_separatrix
items.description:
Net energy power leaving the confined plasma through the last closed
magnetic flux surface and entering the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
Separatrix power is the net global energy loss from the confined plasma into
the scrape-off layer across the last closed magnetic flux surface. It
represents the aggregate power crossing the entire separatrix rather than a
local surface value.

The defining boundary integral is

$$
P_{\rm sep} = \oint_{S_{\rm sep}} \mathbf{S}_E \cdot \hat{\mathbf{n}}\, dA
$$

where $P_{\rm sep}$ is the separatrix power, $S_{\rm sep}$ is the last
closed magnetic flux surface, $\mathbf{S}_E$ is the net plasma-energy flux
density, $\hat{\mathbf{n}}$ is the unit normal directed from the confined
plasma toward the scrape-off layer, and $dA$ is an element of separatrix
area.

This is a total, net quantity integrated over the complete separatrix. It
applies to the confined plasma as a whole, with no selection of species,
reaction channel, or individual transport mechanism; outward energy transfer
is the plasma loss represented by the quantity. It is not a pointwise
energy-flux density or a power associated with a single surface location.

The boundary total is distinct from [radiated power over the core
region](name:radiated_power_over_core_region), which describes
electromagnetic power emitted within the core and is not necessarily equal
to power crossing the separatrix. It is also distinct from [power due to
conduction](name:power_due_to_conduction), which describes
conduction-mediated power deposited on plasma-facing surfaces downstream of
the separatrix.

items.name: toroidal_gyrocenter_frequency
items.description:
Toroidal component of the gyrocenter orbit angular frequency, equal to the
signed rate of gyrocenter advance in toroidal angle φ in the right-handed
cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The toroidal gyrocenter frequency is the toroidal component of gyrocenter
orbit angular frequency in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$
frame, where $R$ is major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is
vertical height. It describes the angular advance of a charged-particle
gyrocenter after averaging over its fast cyclotron gyration.

$$
\omega_{\phi,\mathrm{gc}} = \dot{\phi}_{\mathrm{gc}} = \frac{d\phi_{\mathrm{gc}}}{dt}
$$

where $\omega_{\phi,\mathrm{gc}}$ is the toroidal gyrocenter frequency,
$\phi_{\mathrm{gc}}$ is the gyrocenter toroidal angle, and $t$ is time.
Passing orbits contribute toroidal transit motion, whereas trapped orbits
can contribute toroidal precession. This component complements the [poloidal
gyrocenter frequency](name:poloidal_gyrocenter_frequency) and belongs to the
angular-frequency vector [gyrocenter_frequency](name:gyrocenter_frequency);
unlike [toroidal ion rotation
frequency](name:toroidal_ion_rotation_frequency), it describes individual
gyrocenter orbit motion rather than bulk species rotation.

Sign convention: Positive when the gyrocenter advances in the direction of
increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: radial_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential
items.description:
Radial (R) component of the vacuum magnetic vector potential produced solely
by toroidal-field coil currents in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z)
frame.
items.documentation:
The radial component $A_R$ of the vacuum magnetic vector potential is the
projection of $\mathbf{A}_\mathrm{vac}$ onto the radial direction $\hat{R}$
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame. It represents the
$R$-directed component of the gage-dependent vector potential produced
solely by toroidal-field coil currents.

The component projection is defined by:

$$
A_R = \mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}} \cdot \hat{R}
$$

where $\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is the [vacuum magnetic vector
potential](name:vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential), $\hat{R}$ is the unit
vector in the direction of increasing major radius $R$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle, $Z$ is
vertical height, and $\cdot$ denotes the scalar product.

The source population is the toroidal-field coil current system only.
Contributions from plasma currents and from other external-current systems
are excluded; the quantity is a pointwise scalar component, not a spatial
average, flux-surface average, integral, magnetic-induction component, or
the full [magnetic vector potential](name:magnetic_vector_potential).

The corresponding vacuum magnetic induction $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ is
related to the parent vector by $\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}} = \nabla \times
\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$, with $\nabla \times$ denoting the curl operator.
Replacing $\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ by $\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}} + \nabla
\chi$, where $\chi$ is an arbitrary scalar gage function, changes $A_R$ by
the radial projection of $\nabla \chi$ while leaving
$\mathbf{B}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ unchanged; the [vertical vacuum magnetic vector
potential](name:vertical_vacuum_magnetic_vector_potential) is the analogous
projection along $\hat{Z}$, the vertical basis direction of the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

Sign convention: Positive when $\mathbf{A}_{\mathrm{vac}}$ has a projection
along $+\hat{R}$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: binormal_coordinate_of_toroidal_field_coil
items.description:
Signed displacement of each toroidal-field-coil conductor cross-section
outline vertex along the local Frenet–Serret binormal from the conductor
centerline.
items.documentation:
The binormal coordinate specifies the signed local displacement of a
toroidal-field-coil conductor cross-section outline vertex from the
conductor centerline in the direction perpendicular to both the local
tangent and normal.

$$
b_v = (\mathbf{r}_v-\mathbf{r}_c)\cdot\hat{\mathbf{b}}
$$

where $b_v$ is the binormal coordinate, $\mathbf{r}_v$ is the vertex
position in m, $\mathbf{r}_c$ is the corresponding centerline position in m,
and $\hat{\mathbf{b}}$ is the unit binormal of the local Frenet–Serret
frame. Together with the [normal coordinate of the toroidal field
coil](name:normal_coordinate_of_toroidal_field_coil), it defines the
conductor cross-section outline in the local normal–binormal plane; it is
not a global vertical coordinate.

Sign convention: Positive when the vertex displacement has a component in
the direction of the local Frenet–Serret binormal.

items.name: helium_3_density_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Particle number density of the helium-3 ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local helium-3 ion count per physical volume at that
location. It is summed over all helium-3 ionic charge states.
items.documentation:
Particle number density of the helium-3 ion population evaluated at the
magnetic axis is the local helium-3 ion count per physical volume at that
location. It represents helium-3 ions specifically, rather than neutral
helium-3, electrons, or another plasma population.

The defining relation is

$$
n_{3,\mathrm{axis}} = \left.\frac{dN_3}{dV}\right|_{\mathrm{axis}}
$$

where $n_{3,\mathrm{axis}}$ is the helium-3 ion number density at the
magnetic axis, $N_3$ is the number of helium-3 ions, and $V$ is physical
volume.

The quantity is local to the magnetic axis, the innermost location of nested
closed poloidal magnetic-flux surfaces where the poloidal-flux gradient
vanishes. It applies to the complete helium-3 ion population at that
location and is summed over all helium-3 ionic charge states; it is neither
a flux-surface or volume integral nor a neutral-helium or other-species
density.

This is the helium-3-specific realization of the population-independent
[density at the magnetic axis](name:density_at_magnetic_axis). The
unlocalized [helium-3 density](name:helium_3_density) describes the same
charge-state-summed helium-3 ion population without this specified
magnetic-axis locus, while [helium-4 density at the magnetic
axis](name:helium_4_density_at_magnetic_axis) represents the corresponding
density for a different helium isotope.

items.name: tritium_velocity
items.description:
Tritium velocity is the directed motion of the tritium plasma population at
a physical location, represented by a velocity vector. As a species-level
intensive quantity, it denotes the density-weighted mean velocity over all
tritium charge states.
items.documentation:
Tritium velocity is the fluid velocity vector of the tritium plasma
population at a specified physical location. It is the first velocity moment
of the tritium phase-space distribution and represents motion of the tritium
species as a vector, not a selected coordinate component.

For charge-state-resolved tritium populations, the species-level velocity is
the density-weighted mean over charge states:

$$
\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{T}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T},q}\,\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{T},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{T},q}}
$$

where $q$ labels tritium charge state, $n_{\mathrm{T},q}$ is the number
density of tritium in charge state $q$, and $\mathbf{v}_{\mathrm{T},q}$ is
the velocity vector of tritium in charge state $q$.

It does not by itself select any scalar component or projection; a component
name supplies the associated axis or signed direction. The toroidal tritium
velocity is the projection of this vector onto the toroidal $\hat{\phi}$
direction in the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is
major radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height.

items.name: toroidal_iron_velocity_at_internal_transport_barrier
items.description:
Density-weighted iron-ion bulk-flow velocity along increasing toroidal
angle, averaged over all ionization charge states at the internal transport
barrier.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the bulk velocity of ionized iron
at the flux-surface locus of the internal transport barrier. It is a
density-weighted mean across iron ionization charge states in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $\phi$ is the toroidal
angle.

The charge-state aggregation is defined by

$$
v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}}
$$
