where $q$ is the ionization charge number, $n_{\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is the
number density of iron ions in state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, and
$v_{\phi,\mathrm{Fe}^{q+}}$ is that state's toroidal bulk-flow component in
m.s$^{-1}$. Neutral iron is excluded from the sum.

The internal-transport-barrier value is distinct from the corresponding
values at the [magnetic axis](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_magnetic_axis)
and [pedestal top](name:toroidal_iron_velocity_at_pedestal_top), which use
different flux-surface loci.

Sign convention: Positive when the iron-ion bulk flow points in the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$.

items.name: radial_outline_of_plasma_filament
items.description:
Radial outline of a plasma filament is the major-radius coordinate of each
filament-outline point in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame,
where R is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis.
items.documentation:
Radial outline of a plasma filament is the major-radius coordinate $R$ of
each point on the plasma-filament outline in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, where $R$ is distance from the toroidal symmetry axis
and $Z$ is vertical height. It gives the radial location of the outline
locus and is the filament-outline specialization of the generic [radial
coordinate](name:radial_coordinate).

For an outline point with Cartesian coordinates $(x,y,z)$ in a right-handed
Cartesian frame with basis $(\hat{x}, \hat{y}, \hat{z})$, with the $z$ axis
coincident with the toroidal symmetry axis, the coordinate is defined by:

$$
R = \sqrt{x^2 + y^2}
$$

where $x$ and $y$ are the Cartesian coordinates perpendicular to the
toroidal symmetry axis.

This quantity is a coordinate of each outline point, not a signed radial
vector projection, flux-surface-normal displacement, filament width, or
aggregate radius. It should not be confused with the [outer radius of a
plasma filament](name:outer_radius_of_plasma_filament), which denotes an
outer radial extent rather than the coordinate of an individual outline
point.

items.name: radial_coordinate_of_control_surface
items.description:
Major-radius coordinate of each point on a control-surface outline, measured
as perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry axis in the
right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame.
items.documentation:
The radial coordinate of a control-surface outline point is its major-radius
location, measured as perpendicular distance from the toroidal symmetry
axis. It identifies the point's position in the right-handed cylindrical
$(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

The defining geometric relation is

$$
R = \sqrt{X^2 + Y^2}
$$

where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate, and $X$ and $Y$ are the Cartesian
coordinates perpendicular to the toroidal symmetry axis in the right-handed
Cartesian $(\hat{x},\hat{y},\hat{z})$ basis. The cylindrical angle $\phi$ is
the toroidal angular coordinate and $Z$ is the vertical coordinate of the
same point.

This quantity applies to each point defining the control-surface outline.
The control surface is defined by an outline in a poloidal plane and extends
in the toroidal direction with axisymmetric geometry; this quantity is the
local coordinate of an outline point, not a surface average or an integrated
surface property. It is distinct from displacement along a flux-surface
normal, which describes a different geometric direction.

This entry specializes [radial coordinate](name:radial_coordinate) by
restricting its locus to a point on a control-surface outline while
retaining the same major-radius definition.

items.name: vertical_curvature_of_bragg_crystal
items.description:
Radius of curvature of the diffracting surface of a Bragg crystal along its
local vertical (X2) direction, defining one axis of its focusing geometry.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the local radius of curvature of the Bragg crystal's
diffracting surface along its local vertical, or X2, tangent direction. It
characterizes the crystal bending used for Bragg-diffraction focusing in a
doubly curved geometry.

$$
R_v = \frac{1}{|\kappa_v|}
$$

where $R_v$ is the radius of curvature in m and $\kappa_v$ is the signed
normal curvature in m$^{-1}$ along the local vertical tangent direction. A
planar surface corresponds to zero curvature and an unbounded radius.

This quantity describes the diffracting surface, not the geometric aperture
radius given by [radius of Bragg crystal](name:radius_of_bragg_crystal).
Together with the toroidal curvature of the Bragg crystal, it specifies the
directional curvature scales of a doubly curved crystal.

items.name: radial_outline_of_passive_loop_element
items.description:
Radial outline of a passive-loop element is the major-radius coordinate of
each point on the irregular cross-sectional outline of a passive-loop
conductor element in the right-handed cylindrical (R, φ, Z) frame, where R
is measured from the machine symmetry axis and Z is vertical height.
items.documentation:
Radial outline of a passive-loop element is the major-radius coordinate $R$
of a point on the irregular cross-sectional boundary contour of a
passive-loop conductor element. It is expressed in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is the major-radius coordinate
measured from the machine symmetry axis, $\phi$ is the toroidal angle
increasing counterclockwise when viewed from above, and $Z$ is the vertical
coordinate.

The scope is the boundary contour of the passive-loop conductor element,
evaluated pointwise over the outline rather than as an aggregate over the
element. Because $R$ is a distance from the symmetry axis, it is
non-negative. This quantity is not a radial thickness, a contour length, or
the radial coordinate of a passive-loop element, which denotes a
representative radial location of the element rather than an outline point.

Together with the vertical outline of a passive-loop element, it defines the
$(R,Z)$ position of the same passive-loop boundary contour in a poloidal
cross-section: this quantity supplies $R$, while the vertical outline
supplies $Z$ for the corresponding outline point.

items.name: neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift
items.description:
Vector velocity attributed to a specified species or internal state for
motion associated with crossed local electric and magnetic fields.
items.documentation:
The E×B-drift velocity is the vector velocity attributed to a particle
population or specified internal state for motion associated with crossed
local electric and magnetic fields.

For a nonzero magnetic field, the ideal drift contribution is defined by

$$
\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}=\frac{\mathbf{E}\times\mathbf{B}}{|\mathbf{B}|^2}
$$

where $\mathbf{E}$ is the local electric-field vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the
local magnetic-field vector, and $\mathbf{v}_{E\times B}$ is the attributed
drift velocity. The quantity represents only the E×B-drift contribution and
excludes other drift mechanisms. For neutral internal states, it is an
assigned kinematic velocity associated with the local fields rather than
direct acceleration by the Lorentz force; its vertical component is
represented by [vertical neutral species internal-state E×B-drift
velocity](name:vertical_neutral_species_internal_state_velocity_due_to_e_cross_b_drift).

Sign convention: Positive when a component points along increasing $R$,
$\phi$, or $Z$ in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient
items.description:
Vector of directional diffusion coefficients governing diffusive transport
of bulk-ion momentum in a magnetized plasma, with distinct radial, poloidal,
and toroidal components forming the diagonal of the ion momentum diffusivity
tensor.
items.documentation:
The ion momentum diffusion coefficient vector collects the anisotropic
diagonal components of the bulk-ion momentum diffusivity tensor, each
relating the diffusive flux of bulk-ion momentum along a given geometric
direction to the local gradient of ion momentum density in that direction.
In a gradient-diffusion closure, each directional component $\chi_{\rm mom}$
satisfies the constitutive relation:

$$
\Gamma_{\rm mom} = -\chi_{\rm mom}\,\nabla(m_i n_i v_i)
$$

where $\Gamma_{\rm mom}$ is the diffusive ion momentum flux density, $m_i$
is the ion mass, $n_i$ is the ion number density, and $v_i$ is the bulk ion
flow velocity component in the corresponding direction. The three
projections are radial_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient, governing
cross-flux-surface momentum mixing;
poloidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient, governing transport along the
poloidal direction tangent to flux surfaces; and
toroidal_ion_momentum_diffusion_coefficient, governing diffusion of toroidal
angular momentum. The radial component is the confinement-relevant quantity
and is inferred from toroidal momentum balance analyzes or gyrokinetic and
fluid turbulence simulations. The scalar analog ion_momentum_diffusivity
represents the same physical concept without directional decomposition,
while plasma_momentum_diffusivity extends the concept to the full plasma
mixture.

items.name: ion_field_line_average_temperature_over_scrape_off_layer
items.description:
Ion temperature averaged along an open magnetic field line between upstream
and downstream locations in the scrape-off layer.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the mean bulk-ion thermal temperature along an open
magnetic field line through the scrape-off layer, between specified upstream
and downstream locations. It represents the connected-field-line average
rather than the local temperature at a single position.

The field-line average is defined by

$$
\overline{T}_i = \frac{1}{L_{\parallel}} \int_{s_u}^{s_d} T_i(s)\,ds
$$

where $T_i(s)$ is the local ion temperature, $s$ is arc length along the
magnetic field line, $s_u$ and $s_d$ are the upstream and downstream
endpoints, and $L_{\parallel}=s_d-s_u$ is the connection length. The result
is distinct from the local ion temperature at midplane and does not denote a
flux-surface average.

items.name: curvature_of_arc_of_circle_center
items.description:
Geometric length scale of a curved boundary or line, with larger values
indicating gentler bending and smaller values indicating sharper bending.
items.documentation:
The radius of curvature is the local geometric length associated with the
bending of a curve or boundary. It is the radius of the circle that most
closely represents the curve at the location of interest.

For curvature represented by its non-negative magnitude, the radius of
curvature is defined by

$$
\rho = \frac{1}{\kappa}
$$

where $\rho$ is the radius of curvature and $\kappa$ is the local curvature
magnitude.

This quantity applies to a geometric curve or boundary and is not the
position of the curve's center, its total length, or the full extent of the
object containing it. The [radius of curvature of an arc-of-circle
center](name:curvature_inverse_of_arc_of_circle_center) is a specialized
instance for an iron-core segment boundary; for an exact circular arc,
$\rho$ equals the circle radius and is constant along that arc.

items.name: trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions
items.description:
Trapped thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local
angular-momentum transfer rate to the trapped part of the bulk thermal
electron population from Coulomb collisions.
items.documentation:
Trapped thermal electron torque density due to collisions is the local rate
per unit volume at which Coulomb scattering transfers angular momentum to
the bulk, near-Maxwellian thermal electron population, restricted to the
trapped receiving orbit class.

The vector torque density is defined by

$$
\boldsymbol{\tau}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,trap}} = \frac{d\boldsymbol{L}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,trap}}}{dV\,dt}
$$

where $\boldsymbol{L}_{e,\mathrm{th}}^{\mathrm{coll,trap}}$ is the angular
momentum transferred to trapped thermal electrons by Coulomb collisions, $V$
is physical volume, and $t$ is time.

This quantity is the trapped-orbit contribution to [thermal electron torque
density due to
collisions](name:thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions). The
trapped qualifier identifies the receiving thermal-electron orbit class and
does not restrict the collision partner. It excludes non-Coulomb mechanisms
and torque deposited in non-thermal or non-electron populations. No single
directional component is selected; its toroidal projection is [toroidal
trapped thermal electron torque density due to
collisions](name:toroidal_trapped_thermal_electron_torque_density_due_to_collisions),
with components resolved in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: electron_density_at_plasma_boundary
items.description:
Number density of electrons at the plasma boundary, counting all free
electrons and allowing pointwise values or an explicitly specified
flux-surface average.
items.documentation:
Number density of electron

The local density is defined by

$$
n_e(\mathbf{x}) = \int f_e(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{v})\,d^3v
$$

where $n_e$ is the local electron number density, $\mathbf{x}$ is the
spatial position on the plasma boundary, $\mathbf{v}$ is electron velocity,
$f_e$ is the electron phase-space number distribution, and $d^3v$ is the
velocity-space volume element. The integral covers the full electron
velocity distribution.

The population includes thermal and nonthermal free electrons without an
orbit-class restriction; electrons bound in atoms or ions are excluded.
Unlike [ion density at the plasma
boundary](name:ion_density_at_plasma_boundary), this quantity counts
electrons rather than ions.

This quantity encompasses pointwise values and explicitly specified
magnetic-flux-surface averages. The [flux-surface-averaged electron density
at the plasma
boundary](name:flux_surface_averaged_electron_density_at_plasma_boundary) is
its surface-averaged specialization, using inverse-magnitude
poloidal-flux-gradient weighting rather than pointwise evaluation. Neither a
chord average nor an average over the confined plasma volume is implied.

The last closed magnetic flux surface: the outermost flux surface on which
field lines close on themselves, bounding the confined plasma. Where $\psi =
\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$, $\psi$ is poloidal magnetic flux;
$\psi_{\mathrm{LCFS}}$ is its value on the last closed flux surface.

items.name: perpendicular_normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure
items.description:
Normalized perpendicular pressure-tensor moment of the perturbed particle
distribution for a linear gyrokinetic eigenmode, representing its
perpendicular thermal-energy fluctuation relative to a reference pressure.
items.documentation:
The perpendicular normalized particle perturbed pressure is a dimensionless
complex eigenmode moment of the perturbed particle distribution function. It
represents the fluctuation of thermal energy associated with random particle
motion perpendicular to the background magnetic field and is the
perpendicular component of the [normalized particle perturbed
pressure](name:normalized_particle_perturbed_pressure).

For species $s$, it is defined by the perpendicular second velocity-space
moment:

$$
\hat{p}_{\perp,s} = \frac{m_s}{2p_\mathrm{ref}} \int v_\perp^2\,\delta f_s\,d^3v
$$

where $m_s$ is the species mass, $v_\perp$ is the speed perpendicular to the
background magnetic field, $\delta f_s$ is the perturbed particle
distribution function, $d^3v$ is the velocity-space volume element, and
$p_\mathrm{ref}$ is a positive reference thermal pressure. The perpendicular
and parallel normalized particle perturbed pressure components together
describe the gyrotropic pressure perturbation.

Unlike the perpendicular normalized gyrocenter perturbed pressure, this
moment is formed from the physical particle distribution and includes
finite-Larmor-radius effects associated with the particle-to-gyrocenter
transformation.

Sign convention: Positive when the perpendicular pressure perturbation
represents a local increase in perpendicular thermal energy relative to the
equilibrium background.

items.name: left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part
items.description:
Signed in-phase quadrature of the E-plus, left-hand circular wave
electric-field phasor along a beam or ray path, relative to its chosen phase
reference.
items.documentation:
The quantity is the signed in-phase real quadrature of the complex
[left-hand circularly polarized wave electric
field](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field) phasor,
conventionally called E-plus. It describes the circular polarization
contribution transverse to the local equilibrium magnetic field along an
electron cyclotron emission beam or ray path.

Its defining relation is

$$
E_{+,\mathrm{real}} = \operatorname{Re}(\widetilde{E}_+)
$$

where $E_{+,\mathrm{real}}$ is the signed in-phase quadrature,
$\widetilde{E}_+$ is the complex E-plus electric-field phasor, and
$\operatorname{Re}$ denotes taking the real part.

This is a local polarization quadrature of the wave [electric
field](name:electric_field), not a path-integrated field, phasor magnitude,
intensity, or complete instantaneous electric field. Its value depends on
the chosen transverse polarization basis and phase reference; changing the
phase reference mixes the real and imaginary quadratures.

Together with the [E-plus imaginary
quadrature](name:left_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_imaginary_part),
it reconstructs the complex E-plus phasor. The [right-hand circular real
quadrature](name:right_hand_circularly_polarized_wave_electric_field_real_part)
instead resolves the opposite circular polarization, E-minus.

Sign convention: Positive when the E-plus phasor phase lies within
one-quarter cycle of the chosen in-phase reference, modulo a full cycle.

items.name: minimum_over_flux_surface_magnetic_field_magnitude
items.description:
Smallest total magnetic-field strength attained along a specified nested
magnetic flux surface, using the field magnitude rather than a signed
component.
items.documentation:
The minimum magnetic-field magnitude is the smallest total field strength
attained anywhere on a specified nested magnetic flux surface. It is
sign-invariant because it uses the modulus of the magnetic-field vector
rather than a signed component.

For a surface labeled by the magnetic-flux coordinate $\psi$, the quantity
is defined by

$$
B_{\min}(\psi) = \min_{\mathbf{x} \in S(\psi)} \left|\mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x})\right|
$$

where $B_{\min}(\psi)$ is the minimum magnetic-field magnitude, $\mathbf{x}$
is a position on the surface, $S(\psi)$ is the set of positions belonging to
the flux surface labeled by $\psi$, and $\mathbf{B}(\mathbf{x})$ is the
total magnetic-field vector at that position.

The minimum is taken over all positions on each nested magnetic flux surface
and includes the complete equilibrium field, including its poloidal and
toroidal contributions. It is not a signed component minimum, a flux-surface
average, or a minimum taken across multiple flux surfaces.

Unlike the [flux-surface-averaged inverse square of magnetic-field
magnitude](name:flux_surface_averaged_inverse_of_square_of_magnetic_field_magnitude),
this quantity reduces the field magnitude itself by a pointwise minimum
rather than averaging its reciprocal square.

items.name: torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force
items.description:
Net mechanical torque transferred to plasma particles by the Lorentz force
density, obtained by integrating the moment of j cross B over the plasma
volume.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the net mechanical torque transferred to charged plasma
particles by the electromagnetic Lorentz force. It is a scalar component of
the volume-integrated angular-momentum transfer associated with the current
density and magnetic field.

For a torque component about a specified axis, the defining relation is

$$
\tau_{\hat{a}} = \int_V \left[\mathbf{r} \times \left(\mathbf{j} \times \mathbf{B}\right)\right] \cdot \hat{\mathbf{a}}\,dV
$$

where $\tau_{\hat{a}}$ is the torque component, $\mathbf{r}$ is the position
relative to the torque origin, $\mathbf{j}$ is the electric-current-density
vector, $\mathbf{B}$ is the magnetic-field vector, $\hat{\mathbf{a}}$ is the
unit vector along the selected torque axis, and $V$ is the plasma volume.
The [particle torque due to j cross B
force](name:particle_torque_due_to_j_cross_b_force) is a specific instance
of this quantity. Unlike [toroidal torque density due to j cross B
force](name:toroidal_torque_density_due_to_j_cross_b_force), this parent
denotes a volume-integrated torque rather than a local torque density.

Sign convention: Positive when the Lorentz-force moment points along the
positive direction of the torque axis; for a toroidal component, this is the
direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame.

items.name: alpha_angle_of_antenna_strap
items.description:
Signed inclination of the alpha-side lateral face of an oblique trapezoidal
ICRH antenna-strap cross-section relative to the directed strap base edge.
items.documentation:
The alpha angle is the oriented inclination of the alpha-side lateral face
of an oblique trapezoidal ICRH antenna-strap cross-section, measured from
the directed strap base edge. It specifies the alpha-side geometry
complementary to the beta-side quantity represented by angle of antenna
strap.

$$
\alpha = \operatorname{atan2}\!\left(\hat{n}\cdot(\hat{b}\times\hat{a}),\,\hat{b}\cdot\hat{a}\right)
$$

where $\hat{b}$ is the unit vector along the directed strap base edge,
$\hat{a}$ is the unit vector along the alpha-side lateral face, and
$\hat{n}$ is the positive normal to the oriented cross-sectional plane. The
angle is restricted to the alpha-side face and is distinct from the
beta-side inclination.

Sign convention: Positive when rotation from the directed strap base edge
toward the alpha-side lateral face follows the positive normal of the
oriented strap cross-section.

items.name: poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_constraint_position
items.description:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the constraint position is the signed flux through
a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal symmetry axis and bounded by the
toroidal circle through that position.
items.documentation:
Poloidal magnetic flux at the constraint position is the signed [magnetic
flux](name:magnetic_flux) through a horizontal disk centered on the toroidal
symmetry axis and bounded by the toroidal circle through that position.

In an axisymmetric equilibrium, its defining relation in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame is

$$
\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}(R,Z) = 2\pi \int_0^R B_Z(R',Z)\,R'\,dR'
$$

where $\Phi_{\mathrm{p}}$ is the poloidal magnetic flux, $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, $Z$ is vertical height, $B_Z$ is the
vertical component of the total equilibrium magnetic field, and $R'$ is the
major-radius integration variable. The expression is evaluated at the
constraint position.

This is a point evaluation of [poloidal magnetic
flux](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux), not a spatial average, and includes both
externally generated and plasma-generated contributions. Within a region of
nested magnetic surfaces, it labels the surface passing through that
position and supplies a surface coordinate for transport coefficients and
plasma source terms. Unlike [toroidal magnetic
flux](name:toroidal_magnetic_flux), it is not flux through a poloidal
cross-section.

For plasma current flowing in the direction of increasing $\phi$, the flux
decreases from the [magnetic-axis
value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_magnetic_axis) to the [plasma-boundary
value](name:poloidal_magnetic_flux_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the net magnetic field threading the
horizontal disk is oriented toward increasing $Z$.

items.name: thickness_of_ferritic_element
items.description:
Thickness of a ferritic element is the non-negative face-to-face extent of
its rectangular poloidal cross section in the right-handed cylindrical (R,
φ, Z) frame, where R is major radius, φ is toroidal angle, and Z is vertical
height, measured along the in-plane direction normal to the element
centerline. It is distinct from width along the centerline and from toroidal
extent.
items.documentation:
Thickness of a ferritic element is the non-negative separation between the
two opposing through-thickness faces of the rectangular poloidal cross
section of an axisymmetric ferritic element. In a plane of constant $\phi$
in the right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, where $R$ is major
radius, $\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height, the centerline
is the geometric midline of that rectangle, and the through-thickness
direction is the in-plane direction normal to the centerline.

The thickness $d$ is the absolute face-to-face separation along the
through-thickness normal:

$$
d = \left|(\mathbf{r}_+ - \mathbf{r}_-) \cdot \hat{\mathbf{t}}\right|
$$

where $d$ is the thickness of the ferritic element, $\mathbf{r}_+$ and
$\mathbf{r}_-$ are position vectors of any points on the two opposing
through-thickness faces in the same poloidal cross section, and
$\hat{\mathbf{t}}$ is either unit normal to the centerline within that
poloidal cross section. The absolute value makes the quantity independent of
which face is chosen as the reference face.

The scope is a single rectangular cross section of a ferritic element, and
the physical population is the ferritic material belonging to that element.
Its aggregation convention is one element-level geometric extent for that
rectangle; it is not an average over multiple elements, an average around
the toroidal sweep, or a description of local surface roughness or
non-rectangular shape variation.

The [width of a ferritic element](name:width_of_ferritic_element) is the
extent parallel to the centerline of the same rectangle, whereas this
thickness is the orthogonal in-plane extent across the centerline. For the
ideal rectangular cross section, the poloidal cross-section area equals this
thickness multiplied by that width. The quantity is not a cylindrical
major-radius or vertical extent unless the local through-thickness direction
happens to align with the corresponding direction in the right-handed
cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame, and it is not the toroidal extent of the
axisymmetric element.

items.name: ion_density
items.description:
Local number density of ions at a plasma point is the particle number
density of a specified ion species, charge state, or population; a
species-level quantity without an explicit charge state is summed over all
charge states. It is not electric charge density or mass density.
items.documentation:
Local number density of ions at a plasma point is the particle number
density of the specified ion species, charge state, or population. It counts
ions as particles and is distinct from electric charge density and mass
density. For a species-level quantity without an explicit charge state, the
density is summed over all charge states of that species represented in the
same population scope.

The local differential definition is:

$$
n_i = \frac{dN_i}{dV}
$$

where $n_i$ is the ion number density, $N_i$ is the number of ions in the
specified population, and $V$ is physical volume.

For species $s$, the charge-state-summed convention is $n_{i,s} = \sum_Z
n_{i,s,Z}$, where $n_{i,s,Z}$ is the ion number density of charge state $Z$
within the same species and population scope. A charge-state-resolved
counterpart fixes $Z$ instead of applying this sum; [ion charge-state
density](name:ion_charge_state_density) denotes such a quantity at its own
stated population scope. Population-qualified forms restrict the same
density concept, such as [thermal ion density](name:thermal_ion_density) for
thermal ions and [fast ion density](name:fast_ion_density) for suprathermal
ions, while [total ion density](name:total_ion_number_density) aggregates
over ion species and [volume-averaged ion
density](name:volume_averaged_ion_density) is a spatial average of the local
density.

items.name: ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_3_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density
items.description:
Dimensionless composition ratio comparing the charge-state-summed helium-3
ion density averaged over the confined plasma volume with the electron
density averaged over the same volume. It is the helium-3 average divided by
the electron average.
items.documentation:
Dimensionless composition ratio comparing the charge-state-summed helium-3
ion density averaged over the confined plasma volume with the electron
density averaged over the same volume. It is the helium-3 average divided by
the electron average and represents the global helium-3 ion composition
relative to electrons.

The ratio is defined by applying the volume average separately to each
density over the same confined plasma volume before division:

$$
r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e} =
\frac{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})\,dV}{\frac{1}{V_c}\int_{V_c} n_e(\mathbf{x})\,dV}
$$

where $r_{{}^3\mathrm{He}/e}$ is this composition ratio,
$n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}(\mathbf{x})$ is the local helium-3 ion number density
summed over all charged ionization states, $n_e(\mathbf{x})$ is the local
electron number density, $\mathbf{x}$ denotes position, $dV$ is the volume
element, and $V_c$ is the confined plasma volume, with the same symbol
denoting its volume measure in the normalization factors.

The scope is a species-level, volume-averaged, confined-plasma composition
ratio. The helium-3 population includes charged helium-3 ions summed over
charge states and excludes neutral helium-3 atoms; the electron population
is the corresponding electron population in the same confined volume. No
particular time within an evolution is part of the quantity definition.

This quantity is not the confined-volume average of the local ratio
$n_{{}^3\mathrm{He}}/n_e$; it equals that average only for special spatial
distributions. Its numerator is the [volume-averaged helium-3
density](name:volume_averaged_helium_3_density), and its denominator is the
[volume-averaged electron density](name:volume_averaged_electron_density).
The [ratio of volume-averaged helium-4 density to volume-averaged electron
density](name:ratio_of_volume_averaged_helium_4_density_to_volume_averaged_electron_density)
is the analogous isotope composition ratio for helium-4.

items.name: vertical_diamagnetic_current_density
items.description:
Vertical diamagnetic current density is the signed projection of
pressure-gradient-driven electric current per unit area along the toroidal
symmetry axis in edge plasma.
items.documentation:
Vertical diamagnetic current density is the signed projection of the
diamagnetic contribution to [current density](name:current_density) onto the
direction parallel to the toroidal symmetry axis. It represents
pressure-gradient-driven charge transport in the edge plasma.

The projection is defined by:

$$
j_{\mathrm{dia},Z} = \hat{\mathbf{z}}\cdot\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}
$$

where $j_{\mathrm{dia},Z}$ is the vertical diamagnetic current density,
$\mathbf{j}_{\mathrm{dia}}$ is the [current density due to diamagnetic
drift](name:current_density_due_to_diamagnetic_drift), and
$\hat{\mathbf{z}}$ is the unit vector along increasing vertical height. In
the right-handed cylindrical $(R, \phi, Z)$ frame, $R$ is major radius,
$\phi$ is toroidal angle, and $Z$ is vertical height; $\hat{\mathbf{z}}$
points along increasing $Z$.

This quantity is the local algebraic sum of the vertical diamagnetic-current
contributions from all included charge carriers and charge states; it is not
species- or charge-state-resolved. It includes only the diamagnetic
contribution, not the total vertical plasma current from all mechanisms, and
implies neither spatial averaging nor integration.

The underlying vector has the magnitude given by [diamagnetic current
density](name:diamagnetic_current_density); the vertical projection is
signed and is not that magnitude. It differs from [radial diamagnetic
current density](name:radial_diamagnetic_current_density), which projects
the same vector along increasing major radius, and from [parallel
diamagnetic current density](name:parallel_diamagnetic_current_density),
which projects it along the local magnetic-field direction.

Sign convention: Positive when the diamagnetic current has a component in
the direction of increasing vertical height $Z$.

items.name: trapped_power_density
items.description:
Flux-surface-averaged volumetric energy source rate for the trapped orbit
population, representing energy transfer to or from magnetically bouncing
particles.
items.documentation:
Trapped power density is the flux-surface-averaged rate at which energy is
transferred to or from the trapped orbit population per unit physical
volume. It is the orbit-class specialization of power density for particles
whose parallel motion reverses at magnetic mirror points, so their
guiding-center orbits bounce rather than circulate toroidally.

For a magnetic flux surface, the flux-surface-averaged trapped power density
is defined by

$$
p_{\mathrm{tr}} = \left\langle \frac{dE_{\mathrm{tr}}}{dt\,dV} \right\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}
$$

where $p_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is the trapped power density, $E_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is
the energy transferred to the trapped orbit population, $t$ is time, $V$ is
physical volume, and $\langle\cdot\rangle_{\mathrm{fs}}$ denotes a
flux-surface average over that magnetic flux surface.

The scope is the trapped part of the particle distribution, with
contributions from applicable heating and collisional energy-transfer
processes. The aggregation convention is a net source term over those
processes for the trapped orbit population on the flux surface; it is not a
diagnostic-specific estimate, a point value before flux-surface averaging,
or a total stored energy.

It excludes passing-orbit populations: [co-passing power
density](name:co_passing_power_density) resolves particles circulating in
the co-current direction, and [counter-passing power
density](name:counter_passing_power_density) resolves particles circulating
opposite to that direction. Together, trapped, co-passing, and
counter-passing orbit-class power densities partition the orbit-resolved
contribution to net plasma power density when defined for the same particle
population and energy channels.

Sign convention: Positive when energy is transferred to the trapped orbit
population.

items.name: toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_magnetic_axis
items.description:
Density-weighted toroidal bulk velocity of oxygen ions at the magnetic axis,
averaged over all oxygen ionization states.
items.documentation:
This quantity is the toroidal component of the oxygen-ion bulk flow
evaluated at the magnetic axis, with contributions from all oxygen
ionization states combined as a density-weighted mean.

$$
V_{\phi,\mathrm{O}} = \frac{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O},q} V_{\phi,\mathrm{O},q}}{\sum_q n_{\mathrm{O},q}}
$$

where $q$ indexes oxygen ionization states, $n_{\mathrm{O},q}$ is the number
density of state $q$ in m$^{-3}$, and $V_{\phi,\mathrm{O},q}$ is its
toroidal velocity component in m.s$^{-1}$. The component is defined in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame. The magnetic axis is the
innermost confined-plasma location where the poloidal magnetic-flux gradient
vanishes. Neutral oxygen and other species are excluded. The corresponding
boundary quantity is [toroidal oxygen velocity at the plasma
boundary](name:toroidal_oxygen_velocity_at_plasma_boundary).

Sign convention: Positive when the density-weighted oxygen-ion bulk flow
points in the direction of increasing toroidal angle $\phi$ in the
right-handed cylindrical $(R,\phi,Z)$ frame.

items.name: neutral_power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination
items.description:
Thermal power deposited on divertor targets by recombination reactions of
neutral particles at the plasma-material interface, summed over all targets.
It represents the neutral-particle surface recombination contribution to the
total divertor heat load.
items.documentation:
Neutral recombination power of the divertor is the heat load delivered to
divertor target surfaces when neutral particles undergo recombination
reactions at the plasma-material interface. These reactions include surface
association or recombination of neutral atoms, molecules, or molecular
fragments into more tightly bound neutral species, such as molecule
formation on a material surface. It is the neutral-particle
surface-deposition channel of [total divertor recombination
power](name:power_of_divertor_due_to_recombination).

The full-divertor value is the sum of the corresponding per-target neutral
recombination powers:

$$
P_\mathrm{rec,div}^\mathrm{neutral} = \sum_t P_{\mathrm{rec},t}^\mathrm{neutral}
$$

where $t$ indexes divertor target surfaces and
$P_{\mathrm{rec},t}^\mathrm{neutral}$ is
[neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination](name:neutral_power_at_divertor_target_due_to_recombination)
for target $t$.

This quantity excludes heat delivered by plasma ions, electrons, photons,
conducted or convected plasma energy, and non-recombination neutral
interactions, except for energy deposited through the neutral recombination
process at the target. It is a surface-deposition quantity integrated over
the full divertor assembly, distinct from volumetric
[power_due_to_recombination](name:power_due_to_recombination).

items.name: source_rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion
items.description:
Source rate due to beam-beam fusion is the volume-integrated production rate
of specified fusion reaction products generated by reactions between
energetic ions from beam populations in the plasma. Multiple elements may
represent different products or reaction channels; it is not a
spatial-vector component quantity.
items.documentation:
Source rate due to beam-beam fusion is the volume-integrated rate at which
specified fusion reaction products are produced in the plasma by fusion
reactions between energetic ions belonging to beam populations. The quantity
is product- or channel-resolved as applicable; its vector character denotes
a collection of scalar production rates for selected products or reaction
channels, not components of a geometrical vector.

For a specified product or reaction channel $p$, the corresponding beam-beam
source rate is defined by the volume integral of its local production-rate
density:

$$
\Gamma_p^{\mathrm{bb}} = \int_V s_p^{\mathrm{bb}}(\mathbf{r})\,dV
$$

where $\Gamma_p^{\mathrm{bb}}$ is the source rate due to beam-beam fusion
for product or channel $p$, $s_p^{\mathrm{bb}}(\mathbf{r})$ is the local
volumetric production-rate density of that product or channel due only to
beam-beam fusion at spatial point $\mathbf{r}$, and $V$ is the plasma volume
over which the source is integrated.

The scope is restricted to fusion reactions in which both reacting ions are
energetic ions from beam populations. It excludes fusion involving thermal
ion populations, beam-thermal fusion, total fusion source rates from all
reactant populations, injected beam particle rates, launched or absorbed
beam power, particle flux through a surface, and loss rates of the reaction
products.

The [neutron source rate due to beam-beam
fusion](name:neutron_source_rate_due_to_beam_beam_fusion) is the
specialization for neutron production. If several reaction channels
contribute to the same specified product and are represented separately, the
product total is the sum of the corresponding channel-resolved elements.
